Method: per-file patches from the GitHub PR files API (base 59fb4482ce → HEAD dcc6dcff81), cross-checked against full old files (raw.githubusercontent @59fb4482ce) and full new local files. ## Findings

### SUGGESTION — dynamic_messages.dart:640 — false doc claim / missed dedup
New code (line ~640):
```dart
/// Cancels the no-UI widgets' timers and drops them (shared by
/// [forgetAll] and [dispose]).
void _cancelNoUiTimers() { ... }
```
But `dispose()` (line ~651) still carries its **own inline copy** of the timer-cancel loop (`for (final timer in _noUiTimers.values) { timer.cancel(); } _noUiTimers.clear();`) and was not touched by the PR (the only hunk is `forgetAll`). The doc comment "shared by [forgetAll] and [dispose]" is factually wrong, and the duplicate loop the extraction should have removed is still there. No behavior change — either fix the doc or make `dispose()` call the helper. (Note: `dispose()` also keeps its deliberately *unawaited* `engine.dispose()` loop, which must NOT be merged into the awaited `_disposeEngines` — only the timer loop is the missed dedup.)

### SUGGESTION — unpacked_load_flow.dart:37-42 — inert reordering of pure constructions
Old: `createFolderPicker()` ran first, and when it returned null the function returned **before** `AppsStore(manager.env)` / `UnpackedWidgetLoader(...)` were constructed. New:
```dart
final store = _unpackedStore(manager, appsStore, loader);
final widgetLoader = _unpackedLoader(manager, store, loader);
await _runUnpackedLoad(...); // createFolderPicker() + null-return inside
```
The fallback `AppsStore(manager.env)` and `UnpackedWidgetLoader(env:, appsStore:)` are now constructed even on the no-op host-can't-pick path. Verified both constructors are pure field initializers (`UnpackedWidgetLoader` ctor: `appsStore = appsStore ?? AppsStore(env)`; `AppsStore` ctor assigns platform/readAsset only), so there is no observable behavior change — but the evaluation order did technically change.

### Observation (not a finding) — unpacked_load_flow.dart
The eager `_unpackedStore` also fixes a latent double-construction asymmetry: old code built `AppsStore(manager.env)` once; new code builds it once and passes it to the loader, identical to old. Injection precedence `loader?.appsStore ?? appsStore ?? AppsStore(...)` is byte-identical to old.

Only hunk in the file (+22/−6).
- **catalog_auto_update.dart — CLEAN.** The three passes run in the same order over the same `result.entries`; the shared mutable `updated` list accumulates in identical sequence (pass 1 in-entry order, pass 2 in-entry order, pass 3 skipping `updated.contains(entry.id)` exactly as before); the per-entry try/catch swallow moved into `_reinstallFromCatalog` covers exactly the same statements (download → install → add…

# Apps-cluster review — PR #1881 (chore/1848-crap-app-tier4)

Method: per-file patches from the GitHub PR files API (base 59fb4482ce → HEAD dcc6dcff81), cross-checked against full old files (raw.githubusercontent @59fb4482ce) and full new local files. No `part` files involved in this cluster — all extractions are private helpers in the same library, so no part-registration checks apply.

## Findings

### SUGGESTION — dynamic_messages.dart:640 — false doc claim / missed dedup
New code (line ~640):
```dart
/// Cancels the no-UI widgets' timers and drops them (shared by
/// [forgetAll] and [dispose]).
void _cancelNoUiTimers() { ... }
```
But `dispose()` (line ~651) still carries its **own inline copy** of the timer-cancel loop (`for (final timer in _noUiTimers.values) { timer.cancel(); } _noUiTimers.clear();`) and was not touched by the PR (the only hunk is `forgetAll`). The doc comment "shared by [forgetAll] and [dispose]" is factually wrong, and the duplicate loop the extraction should have removed is still there. No behavior change — either fix the doc or make `dispose()` call the helper. (Note: `dispose()` also keeps its deliberately *unawaited* `engine.dispose()` loop, which must NOT be merged into the awaited `_disposeEngines` — only the timer loop is the missed dedup.)

### SUGGESTION — unpacked_load_flow.dart:37-42 — inert reordering of pure constructions
Old: `createFolderPicker()` ran first, and when it returned null the function returned **before** `AppsStore(manager.env)` / `UnpackedWidgetLoader(...)` were constructed. New:
```dart
final store = _unpackedStore(manager, appsStore, loader);
final widgetLoader = _unpackedLoader(manager, store, loader);
await _runUnpackedLoad(...); // createFolderPicker() + null-return inside
```
The fallback `AppsStore(manager.env)` and `UnpackedWidgetLoader(env:, appsStore:)` are now constructed even on the no-op host-can't-pick path. Verified both constructors are pure field initializers (`UnpackedWidgetLoader` ctor: `appsStore = appsStore ?? AppsStore(env)`; `AppsStore` ctor assigns platform/readAsset only), so there is no observable behavior change — but the evaluation order did technically change.

### Observation (not a finding) — unpacked_load_flow.dart
The eager `_unpackedStore` also fixes a latent double-construction asymmetry: old code built `AppsStore(manager.env)` once; new code builds it once and passes it to the loader, identical to old. Injection precedence `loader?.appsStore ?? appsStore ?? AppsStore(...)` is byte-identical to old.

## File-by-file verification (all semantically identical unless noted above)

- **app_preflight_probe_io.dart — CLEAN.** `_probeJsEngineLibrary()` is called inside the same `try` that held the platform branch; `Platform.isMacOS || Platform.isIOS` evaluated once at the same point; the `on ArgumentError` fallback open stays inside the per-call try in `_probeJavaScriptCore` (a throwing fallback still propagates to the outer `on Object` exactly as before — the fallback open lives in the catch clause in both versions); the outer `on Object` catch swallows exactly the same failure set (nothing new escapes, nothing new is swallowed). QuickJS env-var fallback chain unchanged.
- **apps_store.dart — CLEAN.** `_i18nRefsUnchanged` → `_allI18nRefsUnchanged` + `_i18nRefUnchanged`: same `recorded.entries` iteration order, same first-changed short-circuit, same read+digest comparison (`current != null && _digest(current) == entry.value` ≡ `!(current == null || digest != value)`), `recorded == null → true` preserved. Only hunk in the file (+22/−6).
- **catalog_auto_update.dart — CLEAN.** The three passes run in the same order over the same `result.entries`; the shared mutable `updated` list accumulates in identical sequence (pass 1 in-entry order, pass 2 in-entry order, pass 3 skipping `updated.contains(entry.id)` exactly as before); the per-entry try/catch swallow moved into `_reinstallFromCatalog` covers exactly the same statements (download → install → add…

# Apps-cluster review — PR #1881 (chore/1848-crap-app-tier4)

Method: per-file patches from the GitHub PR files API (base 59fb4482ce → HEAD dcc6dcff81), cross-checked against full old files (raw.githubusercontent @59fb4482ce) and full new local files. No `part` files involved in this cluster — all extractions are private helpers in the same library, so no part-registration checks apply.

## Findings

### SUGGESTION — dynamic_messages.dart:640 — false doc claim / missed dedup
New code (line ~640):
```dart
/// Cancels the no-UI widgets' timers and drops them (shared by
/// [forgetAll] and [dispose]).
void _cancelNoUiTimers() { ... }
```
But `dispose()` (line ~651) still carries its **own inline copy** of the timer-cancel loop (`for (final timer in _noUiTimers.values) { timer.cancel(); } _noUiTimers.clear();`) and was not touched by the PR (the only hunk is `forgetAll`). The doc comment "shared by [forgetAll] and [dispose]" is factually wrong, and the duplicate loop the extraction should have removed is still there. No behavior change — either fix the doc or make `dispose()` call the helper. (Note: `dispose()` also keeps its deliberately *unawaited* `engine.dispose()` loop, which must NOT be merged into the awaited `_disposeEngines` — only the timer loop is the missed dedup.)

### SUGGESTION — unpacked_load_flow.dart:37-42 — inert reordering of pure constructions
Old: `createFolderPicker()` ran first, and when it returned null the function returned **before** `AppsStore(manager.env)` / `UnpackedWidgetLoader(...)` were constructed. New:
```dart
final store = _unpackedStore(manager, appsStore, loader);
final widgetLoader = _unpackedLoader(manager, store, loader);
await _runUnpackedLoad(...); // createFolderPicker() + null-return inside
```
The fallback `AppsStore(manager.env)` and `UnpackedWidgetLoader(env:, appsStore:)` are now constructed even on the no-op host-can't-pick path. Verified both constructors are pure field initializers (`UnpackedWidgetLoader` ctor: `appsStore = appsStore ?? AppsStore(env)`; `AppsStore` ctor assigns platform/readAsset only), so there is no observable behavior change — but the evaluation order did technically change.

### Observation (not a finding) — unpacked_load_flow.dart
The eager `_unpackedStore` also fixes a latent double-construction asymmetry: old code built `AppsStore(manager.env)` once; new code builds it once and passes it to the loader, identical to old. Injection precedence `loader?.appsStore ?? appsStore ?? AppsStore(...)` is byte-identical to old.

## File-by-file verification (all semantically identical unless noted above)

- **app_preflight_probe_io.dart — CLEAN.** `_probeJsEngineLibrary()` is called inside the same `try` that held the platform branch; `Platform.isMacOS || Platform.isIOS` evaluated once at the same point; the `on ArgumentError` fallback open stays inside the per-call try in `_probeJavaScriptCore` (a throwing fallback still propagates to the outer `on Object` exactly as before — the fallback open lives in the catch clause in both versions); the outer `on Object` catch swallows exactly the same failure set (nothing new escapes, nothing new is swallowed). QuickJS env-var fallback chain unchanged.
- **apps_store.dart — CLEAN.** `_i18nRefsUnchanged` → `_allI18nRefsUnchanged` + `_i18nRefUnchanged`: same `recorded.entries` iteration order, same first-changed short-circuit, same read+digest comparison (`current != null && _digest(current) == entry.value` ≡ `!(current == null || digest != value)`), `recorded == null → true` preserved. Only hunk in the file (+22/−6).
- **catalog_auto_update.dart — CLEAN.** The three passes run in the same order over the same `result.entries`; the shared mutable `updated` list accumulates in identical sequence (pass 1 in-entry order, pass 2 in-entry order, pass 3 skipping `updated.contains(entry.id)` exactly as before); the per-entry try/catch swallow moved into `_reinstallFromCatalog` covers exactly the same statements (download → install → add…

Old code inferred the concrete type from `createCalendarService()` at the use site. Compiles fine (flutter_app's analysis_options is plain `flutter_lints`, no `strict-inference`), but it defeats static checking on `calendar.isAvailable` / `calendar.events(...)` inside the extracted methods and deviates from the file's otherwise fully-typed style. ## Findings

### SUGGESTION — dynamic_messages.dart:640 — false doc claim / missed dedup
New code (line ~640):
```dart
/// Cancels the no-UI widgets' timers and drops them (shared by
/// [forgetAll] and [dispose]).
void _cancelNoUiTimers() { ... }
```
But `dispose()` (line ~651) still carries its **own inline copy** of the timer-cancel loop (`for (final timer in _noUiTimers.values) { timer.cancel(); } _noUiTimers.clear();`) and was not touched by the PR (the only hunk is `forgetAll`). The doc comment "shared by [forgetAll] and [dispose]" is factually wrong, and the duplicate loop the extraction should have removed is still there. No behavior change — either fix the doc or make `dispose()` call the helper. (Note: `dispose()` also keeps its deliberately *unawaited* `engine.dispose()` loop, which must NOT be merged into the awaited `_disposeEngines` — only the timer loop is the missed dedup.)

Old: `createFolderPicker()` ran first, and when it returned null the function returned **before** `AppsStore(manager.env)` / `UnpackedWidgetLoader(...)` were constructed. New:
```dart
final store = _unpackedStore(manager, appsStore, loader);

```
The fallback `AppsStore(manager.env)` and `UnpackedWidgetLoader(env:, appsStore:)` are now constructed even on the no-op host-can't-pick path. Verified both constructors are pure field initializers (`UnpackedWidgetLoader` ctor: `appsStore = appsStore ?? AppsStore(env)`; `AppsStore` ctor assigns platform/readAsset only), so there is no observable behavior change — but the evaluation order did technically change.

### Observation (not a finding) — unpacked_load_flow.dart
The eager `_unpackedStore` also fixes a latent double-construction asymmetry: old code built `AppsStore(manager.env)` once; new code builds it once and passes it to the loader, identical to old. Injection precedence `loader?.appsStore ?? appsStore ?? AppsStore(...)` is byte-identical to old.

# PR #1881 review — UI widgets + network cluster (9 files)

Method: no shell available, so diffs were reconstructed by reading full NEW files locally and full OLD files fetched from raw.githubusercontent.com at merge-base 59fb4482ce (repo: IstiN/flutter_agent_harness). - **SUGGESTION** — `flutter_app/lib/ui/widgets/apps_panel.dart` ~line 183 (`_calendarReady(calendar)`) and ~line 190 (`_fetchUpcomingEvents(calendar)`): both new helpers declare the `calendar` parameter with no type (implicit `dynamic`). Old code inferred the concrete type from `createCalendarService()` at the use site. Compiles fine (flutter_app's analysis_options is plain `flutter_lints`, no `strict-inference`), but it defeats static checking on `calendar.isAvailable` / `calendar.events(...)` inside the extracted methods and deviates from the file's otherwise fully-typed style. Should be `CalendarApi calendar` (type is imported via `calendar_service.dart`).

Old inner structure: grow rows (`while (rows.length < cursorRow + h)`) → `fits = cursorCol + w <= crossAxisCount` → `dr`/`dc` scan with `&& fits` short-circuit → mark/add/`cursorCol += w`/break → wrap `if (++cursorCol + w > crossAxisCount) { cursorRow++; cursorCol = 0; }`. New: `_growRows` at the same point in the `while(true)`; `_spanFits` does `if (col + w > crossAxisCount) return false;` (exact negation of the old fits initializer, evaluated before the scan, so the case where `cursorCol` advanced past the row end behaves identically — old loop body ran zero iterations in that case too) then `_rowSegmentOccupied` (same `dc` scan, returns on first occupied, same short-circuit). Row indexing safe: `_growRows` guarantees `rows.length >= cursorRow + h` before `_spanFits` touches `rows[row + dr]`. Wrap condition byte-identical; success path returns `(cursorRow, cursorCol + w)` which the caller destructures — matches old `cursorCol += w; break`. No off-by-one, no infinite-loop change (cursor advancement identical on both paths). `w`/`h` clamping identical.
- **quick_switcher.dart** — contains no fuzzy matching; the recents logic (`_recentNetworkIds`, `i < recents.length && i < 7`, `_digitKeys[i + 3]!`) is untouched. The `_switchTo` change collapses three typed catches into one `on Object` + `_resumeErrorMessage` mapping: StateError→`e.message`, FaNetworkException→`e.message`, else→`'$e'` — same dispatch (the two types are unrelated, so catch order in the old code is preserved by the if-order). `context.mounted` guard moved into `_showResumeError`, checked before every snack, same as old.

# Apps-cluster review — PR #1881 (chore/1848-crap-app-tier4)

Method: per-file patches from the GitHub PR files API (base 59fb4482ce → HEAD dcc6dcff81), cross-checked against full old files (raw.githubusercontent @59fb4482ce) and full new local files. No `part` files involved in this cluster — all extractions are private helpers in the same library, so no part-registration checks apply.

## Findings

### SUGGESTION — dynamic_messages.dart:640 — false doc claim / missed dedup
New code (line ~640):
```dart
/// Cancels the no-UI widgets' timers and drops them (shared by
/// [forgetAll] and [dispose]).
void _cancelNoUiTimers() { ... }
```
But `dispose()` (line ~651) still carries its **own inline copy** of the timer-cancel loop (`for (final timer in _noUiTimers.values) { timer.cancel(); } _noUiTimers.clear();`) and was not touched by the PR (the only hunk is `forgetAll`). The doc comment "shared by [forgetAll] and [dispose]" is factually wrong, and the duplicate loop the extraction should have removed is still there. No behavior change — either fix the doc or make `dispose()` call the helper. (Note: `dispose()` also keeps its deliberately *unawaited* `engine.dispose()` loop, which must NOT be merged into the awaited `_disposeEngines` — only the timer loop is the missed dedup.)

### SUGGESTION — unpacked_load_flow.dart:37-42 — inert reordering of pure constructions
Old: `createFolderPicker()` ran first, and when it returned null the function returned **before** `AppsStore(manager.env)` / `UnpackedWidgetLoader(...)` were constructed. New:
```dart
final store = _unpackedStore(manager, appsStore, loader);
final widgetLoader = _unpackedLoader(manager, store, loader);
await _runUnpackedLoad(...); // createFolderPicker() + null-return inside
```
The fallback `AppsStore(manager.env)` and `UnpackedWidgetLoader(env:, appsStore:)` are now constructed even on the no-op host-can't-pick path. Verified both constructors are pure field initializers (`UnpackedWidgetLoader` ctor: `appsStore = appsStore ?? AppsStore(env)`; `AppsStore` ctor assigns platform/readAsset only), so there is no observable behavior change — but the evaluation order did technically change.

### Observation (not a finding) — unpacked_load_flow.dart
The eager `_unpackedStore` also fixes a latent double-construction asymmetry: old code built `AppsStore(manager.env)` once; new code builds it once and passes it to the loader, identical to old. Injection precedence `loader?.appsStore ?? appsStore ?? AppsStore(...)` is byte-identical to old.

## File-by-file verification (all semantically identical unless noted above)

- **app_preflight_probe_io.dart — CLEAN.** `_probeJsEngineLibrary()` is called inside the same `try` that held the platform branch; `Platform.isMacOS || Platform.isIOS` evaluated once at the same point; the `on ArgumentError` fallback open stays inside the per-call try in `_probeJavaScriptCore` (a throwing fallback still propagates to the outer `on Object` exactly as before — the fallback open lives in the catch clause in both versions); the outer `on Object` catch swallows exactly the same failure set (nothing new escapes, nothing new is swallowed). QuickJS env-var fallback chain unchanged.
- **apps_store.dart — CLEAN.** `_i18nRefsUnchanged` → `_allI18nRefsUnchanged` + `_i18nRefUnchanged`: same `recorded.entries` iteration order, same first-changed short-circuit, same read+digest comparison (`current != null && _digest(current) == entry.value` ≡ `!(current == null || digest != value)`), `recorded == null → true` preserved. Only hunk in the file (+22/−6).
- **catalog_auto_update.dart — CLEAN.** The three passes run in the same order over the same `result.entries`; the shared mutable `updated` list accumulates in identical sequence (pass 1 in-entry order, pass 2 in-entry order, pass 3 skipping `updated.contains(entry.id)` exactly as before); the per-entry try/catch swallow moved into `_reinstallFromCatalog` covers exactly the same statements (download → install → add…

Old code inferred the concrete type from `createCalendarService()` at the use site. Compiles fine (flutter_app's analysis_options is plain `flutter_lints`, no `strict-inference`), but it defeats static checking on `calendar.isAvailable` / `calendar.events(...)` inside the extracted methods and deviates from the file's otherwise fully-typed style. Should be `CalendarApi calendar` (type is imported via `calendar_service.dart`).

Row indexing safe: `_growRows` guarantees `rows.length >= cursorRow + h` before `_spanFits` touches `rows[row + dr]`. Wrap condition byte-identical; success path returns `(cursorRow, cursorCol + w)` which the caller destructures — matches old `cursorCol += w; break`. No off-by-one, no infinite-loop change (cursor advancement identical on both paths). `w`/`h` clamping identical.

# Apps-cluster review — PR #1881 (chore/1848-crap-app-tier4)

Method: per-file patches from the GitHub PR files API (base 59fb4482ce → HEAD dcc6dcff81), cross-checked against full old files (raw.githubusercontent @59fb4482ce) and full new local files. No `part` files involved in this cluster — all extractions are private helpers in the same library, so no part-registration checks apply.

## Findings

### SUGGESTION — dynamic_messages.dart:640 — false doc claim / missed dedup
New code (line ~640):
```dart
/// Cancels the no-UI widgets' timers and drops them (shared by
/// [forgetAll] and [dispose]).
void _cancelNoUiTimers() { ... }
```
But `dispose()` (line ~651) still carries its **own inline copy** of the timer-cancel loop (`for (final timer in _noUiTimers.values) { timer.cancel(); } _noUiTimers.clear();`) and was not touched by the PR (the only hunk is `forgetAll`). The doc comment "shared by [forgetAll] and [dispose]" is factually wrong, and the duplicate loop the extraction should have removed is still there. No behavior change — either fix the doc or make `dispose()` call the helper. (Note: `dispose()` also keeps its deliberately *unawaited* `engine.dispose()` loop, which must NOT be merged into the awaited `_disposeEngines` — only the timer loop is the missed dedup.)

### SUGGESTION — unpacked_load_flow.dart:37-42 — inert reordering of pure constructions
Old: `createFolderPicker()` ran first, and when it returned null the function returned **before** `AppsStore(manager.env)` / `UnpackedWidgetLoader(...)` were constructed. New:
```dart
final store = _unpackedStore(manager, appsStore, loader);
final widgetLoader = _unpackedLoader(manager, store, loader);
await _runUnpackedLoad(...); // createFolderPicker() + null-return inside
```
The fallback `AppsStore(manager.env)` and `UnpackedWidgetLoader(env:, appsStore:)` are now constructed even on the no-op host-can't-pick path. Verified both constructors are pure field initializers (`UnpackedWidgetLoader` ctor: `appsStore = appsStore ?? AppsStore(env)`; `AppsStore` ctor assigns platform/readAsset only), so there is no observable behavior change — but the evaluation order did technically change.

### Observation (not a finding) — unpacked_load_flow.dart

# PR #1881 review — UI widgets + network cluster (9 files)

Method: no shell available, so diffs were reconstructed by reading full NEW files locally and full OLD files fetched from raw.githubusercontent.com at merge-base 59fb4482ce (repo: IstiN/flutter_agent_harness). Verified per file: statement order, loop boundaries, short-circuit/early-return conditions, error paths/strings, closure captures, mutable-state threading, dropped/duplicated statements, defaults, string formatting. No `part`/`part of` splits were introduced in this cluster — all extractions are in-place private helpers, so no registration gaps possible.

## Findings

- **SUGGESTION** — `flutter_app/lib/ui/widgets/apps_panel.dart` ~line 183 (`_calendarReady(calendar)`) and ~line 190 (`_fetchUpcomingEvents(calendar)`): both new helpers declare the `calendar` parameter with no type (implicit `dynamic`). Old code inferred the concrete type from `createCalendarService()` at the use site. Compiles fine (flutter_app's analysis_options is plain `flutter_lints`, no `strict-inference`), but it defeats static checking on `calendar.isAvailable` / `calendar.events(...)` inside the extracted methods and deviates from the file's otherwise fully-typed style. Should be `CalendarApi calendar` (type is imported via `calendar_service.dart`).

## Detail checks the assignment called out

- **span_grid_delegate.dart `_packSpan`** — traced exhaustively, EQUIVALENT. Old inner structure: grow rows (`while (rows.length < cursorRow + h)`) → `fits = cursorCol + w <= crossAxisCount` → `dr`/`dc` scan with `&& fits` short-circuit → mark/add/`cursorCol += w`/break → wrap `if (++cursorCol + w > crossAxisCount) { cursorRow++; cursorCol = 0; }`. Old code inferred the concrete type from `createCalendarService()` at the use site. Compiles fine (flutter_app's analysis_options is plain `flutter_lints`, no `strict-inference`), but it defeats static checking on `calendar.isAvailable` / `calendar.events(...)` inside the extracted methods and deviates from the file's otherwise fully-typed style. Should be `CalendarApi calendar` (type is imported via `calendar_service.dart`).

Old inner structure: grow rows (`while (rows.length < cursorRow + h)`) → `fits = cursorCol + w <= crossAxisCount` → `dr`/`dc` scan with `&& fits` short-circuit → mark/add/`cursorCol += w`/break → wrap `if (++cursorCol + w > crossAxisCount) { cursorRow++; cursorCol = 0; }`. # Apps-cluster review — PR #1881 (chore/1848-crap-app-tier4)

Method: per-file patches from the GitHub PR files API (base 59fb4482ce → HEAD dcc6dcff81), cross-checked against full old files (raw.githubusercontent @59fb4482ce) and full new local files. No `part` files involved in this cluster — all extractions are private helpers in the same library, so no part-registration checks apply.

## Findings

### SUGGESTION — dynamic_messages.dart:640 — false doc claim / missed dedup
New code (line ~640):
```dart
/// Cancels the no-UI widgets' timers and drops them (shared by
/// [forgetAll] and [dispose]).
void _cancelNoUiTimers() { ... }
```
But `dispose()` (line ~651) still carries its **own inline copy** of the timer-cancel loop (`for (final timer in _noUiTimers.values) { timer.cancel(); } _noUiTimers.clear();`) and was not touched by the PR (the only hunk is `forgetAll`). The doc comment "shared by [forgetAll] and [dispose]" is factually wrong, and the duplicate loop the extraction should have removed is still there. No behavior change — either fix the doc or make `dispose()` call the helper. (Note: `dispose()` also keeps its deliberately *unawaited* `engine.dispose()` loop, which must NOT be merged into the awaited `_disposeEngines` — only the timer loop is the missed dedup.)

### SUGGESTION — unpacked_load_flow.dart:37-42 — inert reordering of pure constructions
Old: `createFolderPicker()` ran first, and when it returned null the function returned **before** `AppsStore(manager.env)` / `UnpackedWidgetLoader(...)` were constructed. New:
```dart
final store = _unpackedStore(manager, appsStore, loader);
final widgetLoader = _unpackedLoader(manager, store, loader);
await _runUnpackedLoad(...); // createFolderPicker() + null-return inside
```
The fallback `AppsStore(manager.env)` and `UnpackedWidgetLoader(env:, appsStore:)` are now constructed even on the no-op host-can't-pick path. Verified both constructors are pure field initializers (`UnpackedWidgetLoader` ctor: `appsStore = appsStore ?? AppsStore(env)`; `AppsStore` ctor assigns platform/readAsset only), so there is no observable behavior change — but the evaluation order did technically change.

### Observation (not a finding) — unpacked_load_flow.dart
The eager `_unpackedStore` also fixes a latent double-construction asymmetry: old code built `AppsStore(manager.env)` once; new code builds it once and passes it to the loader, identical to old. Injection precedence `loader?.appsStore ?? appsStore ?? AppsStore(...)` is byte-identical to old.

## File-by-file verification (all semantically identical unless noted above)

- **app_preflight_probe_io.dart — CLEAN.** `_probeJsEngineLibrary()` is called inside the same `try` that held the platform branch; `Platform.isMacOS || Platform.isIOS` evaluated once at the same point; the `on ArgumentError` fallback open stays inside the per-call try in `_probeJavaScriptCore` (a throwing fallback still propagates to the outer `on Object` exactly as before — the fallback open lives in the catch clause in both versions); the outer `on Object` catch swallows exactly the same failure set (nothing new escapes, nothing new is swallowed). QuickJS env-var fallback chain unchanged.
- **apps_store.dart — CLEAN.** `_i18nRefsUnchanged` → `_allI18nRefsUnchanged` + `_i18nRefUnchanged`: same `recorded.entries` iteration order, same first-changed short-circuit, same read+digest comparison (`current != null && _digest(current) == entry.value` ≡ `!(current == null || digest != value)`), `recorded == null → true` preserved. Only hunk in the file (+22/−6).
- **catalog_auto_update.dart — CLEAN.** The three passes run in the same order over the same `result.entries`; the shared mutable `updated` list accumulates in identical sequence (pass 1 in-entry order, pass 2 in-entry order, pass 3 skipping `updated.contains(entry.id)` exactly as before); the per-entry try/catch swallow moved into `_reinstallFromCatalog` covers exactly the same statements (download → install → add…

# Apps-cluster review — PR #1881 (chore/1848-crap-app-tier4)

Method: per-file patches from the GitHub PR files API (base 59fb4482ce → HEAD dcc6dcff81), cross-checked against full old files (raw.githubusercontent @59fb4482ce) and full new local files. No `part` files involved in this cluster — all extractions are private helpers in the same library, so no part-registration checks apply.

## Findings

### SUGGESTION — dynamic_messages.dart:640 — false doc claim / missed dedup
New code (line ~640):
```dart
/// Cancels the no-UI widgets' timers and drops them (shared by
/// [forgetAll] and [dispose]).
void _cancelNoUiTimers() { ... }
```
But `dispose()` (line ~651) still carries its **own inline copy** of the timer-cancel loop (`for (final timer in _noUiTimers.values) { timer.cancel(); } _noUiTimers.clear();`) and was not touched by the PR (the only hunk is `forgetAll`). The doc comment "shared by [forgetAll] and [dispose]" is factually wrong, and the duplicate loop the extraction should have removed is still there. No behavior change — either fix the doc or make `dispose()` call the helper. (Note: `dispose()` also keeps its deliberately *unawaited* `engine.dispose()` loop, which must NOT be merged into the awaited `_disposeEngines` — only the timer loop is the missed dedup.)

### SUGGESTION — unpacked_load_flow.dart:37-42 — inert reordering of pure constructions
Old: `createFolderPicker()` ran first, and when it returned null the function returned **before** `AppsStore(manager.env)` / `UnpackedWidgetLoader(...)` were constructed. New:
```dart
final store = _unpackedStore(manager, appsStore, loader);
final widgetLoader = _unpackedLoader(manager, store, loader);
await _runUnpackedLoad(...); // createFolderPicker() + null-return inside
```
The fallback `AppsStore(manager.env)` and `UnpackedWidgetLoader(env:, appsStore:)` are now constructed even on the no-op host-can't-pick path. Verified both constructors are pure field initializers (`UnpackedWidgetLoader` ctor: `appsStore = appsStore ?? AppsStore(env)`; `AppsStore` ctor assigns platform/readAsset only), so there is no observable behavior change — but the evaluation order did technically change.

### Observation (not a finding) — unpacked_load_flow.dart

# PR #1881 review — UI widgets + network cluster (9 files)

Method: no shell available, so diffs were reconstructed by reading full NEW files locally and full OLD files fetched from raw.githubusercontent.com at merge-base 59fb4482ce (repo: IstiN/flutter_agent_harness). Verified per file: statement order, loop boundaries, short-circuit/early-return conditions, error paths/strings, closure captures, mutable-state threading, dropped/duplicated statements, defaults, string formatting. No `part`/`part of` splits were introduced in this cluster — all extractions are in-place private helpers, so no registration gaps possible.

## Findings

- **SUGGESTION** — `flutter_app/lib/ui/widgets/apps_panel.dart` ~line 183 (`_calendarReady(calendar)`) and ~line 190 (`_fetchUpcomingEvents(calendar)`): both new helpers declare the `calendar` parameter with no type (implicit `dynamic`). Old code inferred the concrete type from `createCalendarService()` at the use site. Compiles fine (flutter_app's analysis_options is plain `flutter_lints`, no `strict-inference`), but it defeats static checking on `calendar.isAvailable` / `calendar.events(...)` inside the extracted methods and deviates from the file's otherwise fully-typed style. Should be `CalendarApi calendar` (type is imported via `calendar_service.dart`).

## Detail checks the assignment called out

- **span_grid_delegate.dart `_packSpan`** — traced exhaustively, EQUIVALENT. Old inner structure: grow rows (`while (rows.length < cursorRow + h)`) → `fits = cursorCol + w <= crossAxisCount` → `dr`/`dc` scan with `&& fits` short-circuit → mark/add/`cursorCol += w`/break → wrap `if (++cursorCol + w > crossAxisCount) { cursorRow++; cursorCol = 0; }`. New: `_growRows` at the same point in the `while(true)`; `_spanFits` does `if (col + w > crossAxisCount) return false;` (exact negation of the old fits initializer, evaluated before the scan, so the case where `cursorCol` advanced past the row end behaves identically — old loop body ran zero iterations in that case too) then `_rowSegmentOccupied` (same `dc` scan, returns on first occupied, same short-circuit). Row indexing safe: `_growRows` guarantees `rows.length >= cursorRow + h` before `_spanFits` touches `rows[row + dr]`. Wrap condition byte-identical; success path returns `(cursorRow, cursorCol + w)` which the caller destructures — matches old `cursorCol += w; break`. No off-by-one, no infinite-loop change (cursor advancement identical on both paths). `w`/`h` clamping identical.
- **quick_switcher.dart** — contains no fuzzy matching; the recents logic (`_recentNetworkIds`, `i < recents.length && i < 7`, `_digitKeys[i + 3]!`) is untouched. The `_switchTo` change collapses three typed catches into one `on Object` + `_resumeErrorMessage` mapping: StateError→`e.message`, FaNetworkException→`e.message`, else→`'$e'` — same dispatch (the two types are unrelated, so catch order in the old code is preserved by the if-order). `context.mounted` guard moved into `_showResumeError`, checked before every snack, same as old.
- **file_preview.dart** — no filter logic exists here; extension dispatch verified: stat→mounted→error→`_size` assign→size cap→read→mounted→error→image-ext sniff (`sniffsAsImage`)→audio→video→binary (`_looksBinary`)→utf8/truncate/`_richKindFor`. ```dart
/// Cancels the no-UI widgets' timers and drops them (shared by

void _cancelNoUiTimers() { ... }
```
But `dispose()` (line ~651) still carries its **own inline copy** of the timer-cancel loop (`for (final timer in _noUiTimers.values) { timer.cancel(); } _noUiTimers.clear();`) and was not touched by the PR (the only hunk is `forgetAll`). The doc comment "shared by [forgetAll] and [dispose]" is factually wrong, and the duplicate loop the extraction should have removed is still there. No behavior change — either fix the doc or make `dispose()` call the helper. The fallback `AppsStore(manager.env)` and `UnpackedWidgetLoader(env:, appsStore:)` are now constructed even on the no-op host-can't-pick path. Verified both constructors are pure field initializers (`UnpackedWidgetLoader` ctor: `appsStore = appsStore ?? AppsStore(env)`; `AppsStore` ctor assigns platform/readAsset only), so there is no observable behavior change — but the evaluation order did technically change.

### Observation (not a finding) — unpacked_load_flow.dart
The eager `_unpackedStore` also fixes a latent double-construction asymmetry: old code built `AppsStore(manager.env)` once; new code builds it once and passes it to the loader, identical to old. Injection precedence `loader?.appsStore ?? appsStore ?? AppsStore(...)` is byte-identical to old.

```dart
/// Cancels the no-UI widgets' timers and drops them (shared by
/// [forgetAll] and [dispose]).
void _cancelNoUiTimers() { ... }
```
But `dispose()` (line ~651) still carries its **own inline copy** of the timer-cancel loop (`for (final timer in _noUiTimers.values) { timer.cancel(); } _noUiTimers.clear();`) and was not touched by the PR (the only hunk is `forgetAll`). The doc comment "shared by [forgetAll] and [dispose]" is factually wrong, and the duplicate loop the extraction should have removed is still there. No behavior change — either fix the doc or make `dispose()` call the helper. (Note: `dispose()` also keeps its deliberately *unawaited* `engine.dispose()` loop, which must NOT be merged into the awaited `_disposeEngines` — only the timer loop is the missed dedup.)

```dart

final widgetLoader = _unpackedLoader(manager, store, loader);

```

Verified both constructors are pure field initializers (`UnpackedWidgetLoader` ctor: `appsStore = appsStore ?? AppsStore(env)`; `AppsStore` ctor assigns platform/readAsset only), so there is no observable behavior change — but the evaluation order did technically change.

### Observation (not a finding) — unpacked_load_flow.dart
The eager `_unpackedStore` also fixes a latent double-construction asymmetry: old code built `AppsStore(manager.env)` once; new code builds it once and passes it to the loader, identical to old. Injection precedence `loader?.appsStore ?? appsStore ?? AppsStore(...)` is byte-identical to old.

# PR #1881 review — UI widgets + network cluster (9 files)

Method: no shell available, so diffs were reconstructed by reading full NEW files locally and full OLD files fetched from raw.githubusercontent.com at merge-base 59fb4482ce (repo: IstiN/flutter_agent_harness). Verified per file: statement order, loop boundaries, short-circuit/early-return conditions, error paths/strings, closure captures, mutable-state threading, dropped/duplicated statements, defaults, string formatting. No `part`/`part of` splits were introduced in this cluster — all extractions are in-place private helpers, so no registration gaps possible.

## Findings

- **SUGGESTION** — `flutter_app/lib/ui/widgets/apps_panel.dart` ~line 183 (`_calendarReady(calendar)`) and ~line 190 (`_fetchUpcomingEvents(calendar)`): both new helpers declare the `calendar` parameter with no type (implicit `dynamic`). Old code inferred the concrete type from `createCalendarService()` at the use site. Compiles fine (flutter_app's analysis_options is plain `flutter_lints`, no `strict-inference`), but it defeats static checking on `calendar.isAvailable` / `calendar.events(...)` inside the extracted methods and deviates from the file's otherwise fully-typed style. Should be `CalendarApi calendar` (type is imported via `calendar_service.dart`).

## Detail checks the assignment called out

- **span_grid_delegate.dart `_packSpan`** — traced exhaustively, EQUIVALENT. Old inner structure: grow rows (`while (rows.length < cursorRow + h)`) → `fits = cursorCol + w <= crossAxisCount` → `dr`/`dc` scan with `&& fits` short-circuit → mark/add/`cursorCol += w`/break → wrap `if (++cursorCol + w > crossAxisCount) { cursorRow++; cursorCol = 0; }`. New: `_growRows` at the same point in the `while(true)`; `_spanFits` does `if (col + w > crossAxisCount) return false;` (exact negation of the old fits initializer, evaluated before the scan, so the case where `cursorCol` advanced past the row end behaves identically — old loop body ran zero iterations in that case too) then `_rowSegmentOccupied` (same `dc` scan, returns on first occupied, same short-circuit). Row indexing safe: `_growRows` guarantees `rows.length >= cursorRow + h` before `_spanFits` touches `rows[row + dr]`. Wrap condition byte-identical; success path returns `(cursorRow, cursorCol + w)` which the caller destructures — matches old `cursorCol += w; break`. No off-by-one, no infinite-loop change (cursor advancement identical on both paths). `w`/`h` clamping identical.
- **quick_switcher.dart** — contains no fuzzy matching; the recents logic (`_recentNetworkIds`, `i < recents.length && i < 7`, `_digitKeys[i + 3]!`) is untouched. The `_switchTo` change collapses three typed catches into one `on Object` + `_resumeErrorMessage` mapping: StateError→`e.message`, FaNetworkException→`e.message`, else→`'$e'` — same dispatch (the two types are unrelated, so catch order in the old code is preserved by the if-order). `context.mounted` guard moved into `_showResumeError`, checked before every snack, same as old.
- **file_preview.dart** — no filter logic exists here; extension dispatch verified: stat→mounted→error→`_size` assign→size cap→read→mounted→error→image-ext sniff (`sniffsAsImage`)→audio→video→binary (`_looksBinary`)→utf8/truncate/`_richKindFor`. Order and all caps/defaults unchanged; image branch correctly converted from early-`return` to if/else (no fall-through added).
- **github_connect_sheet.dart** — error-path strings unchanged everywhere: PAT catch → `error.message` / `error.toString()`; scope failure → `context.l10n.githubTokenNoRepoScope`; device flow → `_deviceFlowFailed` (endpointDisabled switches to token tab, else plain error) / `_deviceFlowFailedGeneric` (`error.toString()`, `_deviceStatus = null`) — bodies byte-identical to the old inline catches. The l10n closure in `_tokenConnectFailed(() => context.l10n...)` is invoked only under the `mounted` guard inside setState, matching the old `if (mounted)` blocks.

# Apps-cluster review — PR #1881 (chore/1848-crap-app-tier4)

Method: per-file patches from the GitHub PR files API (base 59fb4482ce → HEAD dcc6dcff81), cross-checked against full old files (raw.githubusercontent @59fb4482ce) and full new local files. No `part` files involved in this cluster — all extractions are private helpers in the same library, so no part-registration checks apply.

## Findings

### SUGGESTION — dynamic_messages.dart:640 — false doc claim / missed dedup
New code (line ~640):
```dart
/// Cancels the no-UI widgets' timers and drops them (shared by
/// [forgetAll] and [dispose]).
void _cancelNoUiTimers() { ... }
```
But `dispose()` (line ~651) still carries its **own inline copy** of the timer-cancel loop (`for (final timer in _noUiTimers.values) { timer.cancel(); } _noUiTimers.clear();`) and was not touched by the PR (the only hunk is `forgetAll`). The doc comment "shared by [forgetAll] and [dispose]" is factually wrong, and the duplicate loop the extraction should have removed is still there. No behavior change — either fix the doc or make `dispose()` call the helper. (Note: `dispose()` also keeps its deliberately *unawaited* `engine.dispose()` loop, which must NOT be merged into the awaited `_disposeEngines` — only the timer loop is the missed dedup.)

### SUGGESTION — unpacked_load_flow.dart:37-42 — inert reordering of pure constructions
Old: `createFolderPicker()` ran first, and when it returned null the function returned **before** `AppsStore(manager.env)` / `UnpackedWidgetLoader(...)` were constructed. New:
```dart
final store = _unpackedStore(manager, appsStore, loader);
final widgetLoader = _unpackedLoader(manager, store, loader);
await _runUnpackedLoad(...); // createFolderPicker() + null-return inside
```
The fallback `AppsStore(manager.env)` and `UnpackedWidgetLoader(env:, appsStore:)` are now constructed even on the no-op host-can't-pick path. Verified both constructors are pure field initializers (`UnpackedWidgetLoader` ctor: `appsStore = appsStore ?? AppsStore(env)`; `AppsStore` ctor assigns platform/readAsset only), so there is no observable behavior change — but the evaluation order did technically change.

### Observation (not a finding) — unpacked_load_flow.dart

# PR #1881 review — UI widgets + network cluster (9 files)

Method: no shell available, so diffs were reconstructed by reading full NEW files locally and full OLD files fetched from raw.githubusercontent.com at merge-base 59fb4482ce (repo: IstiN/flutter_agent_harness). Verified per file: statement order, loop boundaries, short-circuit/early-return conditions, error paths/strings, closure captures, mutable-state threading, dropped/duplicated statements, defaults, string formatting. No `part`/`part of` splits were introduced in this cluster — all extractions are in-place private helpers, so no registration gaps possible.

## Findings

- **SUGGESTION** — `flutter_app/lib/ui/widgets/apps_panel.dart` ~line 183 (`_calendarReady(calendar)`) and ~line 190 (`_fetchUpcomingEvents(calendar)`): both new helpers declare the `calendar` parameter with no type (implicit `dynamic`). Old code inferred the concrete type from `createCalendarService()` at the use site. Compiles fine (flutter_app's analysis_options is plain `flutter_lints`, no `strict-inference`), but it defeats static checking on `calendar.isAvailable` / `calendar.events(...)` inside the extracted methods and deviates from the file's otherwise fully-typed style. Should be `CalendarApi calendar` (type is imported via `calendar_service.dart`).

## Detail checks the assignment called out

- **span_grid_delegate.dart `_packSpan`** — traced exhaustively, EQUIVALENT. Old inner structure: grow rows (`while (rows.length < cursorRow + h)`) → `fits = cursorCol + w <= crossAxisCount` → `dr`/`dc` scan with `&& fits` short-circuit → mark/add/`cursorCol += w`/break → wrap `if (++cursorCol + w > crossAxisCount) { cursorRow++; cursorCol = 0; }`. New: `_growRows` at the same point in the `while(true)`; `_spanFits` does `if (col + w > crossAxisCount) return false;` (exact negation of the old fits initializer, evaluated before the scan, so the case where `cursorCol` advanced past the row end behaves identically — old loop body ran zero iterations in that case too) then `_rowSegmentOccupied` (same `dc` scan, returns on first occupied, same short-circuit). Row indexing safe: `_growRows` guarantees `rows.length >= cursorRow + h` before `_spanFits` touches `rows[row + dr]`. Wrap condition byte-identical; success path returns `(cursorRow, cursorCol + w)` which the caller destructures — matches old `cursorCol += w; break`. No off-by-one, no infinite-loop change (cursor advancement identical on both paths). `w`/`h` clamping identical.
- **quick_switcher.dart** — contains no fuzzy matching; the recents logic (`_recentNetworkIds`, `i < recents.length && i < 7`, `_digitKeys[i + 3]!`) is untouched. The `_switchTo` change collapses three typed catches into one `on Object` + `_resumeErrorMessage` mapping: StateError→`e.message`, FaNetworkException→`e.message`, else→`'$e'` — same dispatch (the two types are unrelated, so catch order in the old code is preserved by the if-order). `context.mounted` guard moved into `_showResumeError`, checked before every snack, same as old.
- **file_preview.dart** — no filter logic exists here; extension dispatch verified: stat→mounted→error→`_size` assign→size cap→read→mounted→error→image-ext sniff (`sniffsAsImage`)→audio→video→binary (`_looksBinary`)→utf8/truncate/`_richKindFor`. ```dart
/// Cancels the no-UI widgets' timers and drops them (shared by

void _cancelNoUiTimers() { ... }
```
But `dispose()` (line ~651) still carries its **own inline copy** of the timer-cancel loop (`for (final timer in _noUiTimers.values) { timer.cancel(); } _noUiTimers.clear();`) and was not touched by the PR (the only hunk is `forgetAll`). The doc comment "shared by [forgetAll] and [dispose]" is factually wrong, and the duplicate loop the extraction should have removed is still there. No behavior change — either fix the doc or make `dispose()` call the helper. The fallback `AppsStore(manager.env)` and `UnpackedWidgetLoader(env:, appsStore:)` are now constructed even on the no-op host-can't-pick path. Verified both constructors are pure field initializers (`UnpackedWidgetLoader` ctor: `appsStore = appsStore ?? AppsStore(env)`; `AppsStore` ctor assigns platform/readAsset only), so there is no observable behavior change — but the evaluation order did technically change.

### Observation (not a finding) — unpacked_load_flow.dart
The eager `_unpackedStore` also fixes a latent double-construction asymmetry: old code built `AppsStore(manager.env)` once; new code builds it once and passes it to the loader, identical to old. Injection precedence `loader?.appsStore ?? appsStore ?? AppsStore(...)` is byte-identical to old.

```dart
/// Cancels the no-UI widgets' timers and drops them (shared by
/// [forgetAll] and [dispose]).
void _cancelNoUiTimers() { ... }
```
But `dispose()` (line ~651) still carries its **own inline copy** of the timer-cancel loop (`for (final timer in _noUiTimers.values) { timer.cancel(); } _noUiTimers.clear();`) and was not touched by the PR (the only hunk is `forgetAll`). The doc comment "shared by [forgetAll] and [dispose]" is factually wrong, and the duplicate loop the extraction should have removed is still there. No behavior change — either fix the doc or make `dispose()` call the helper. (Note: `dispose()` also keeps its deliberately *unawaited* `engine.dispose()` loop, which must NOT be merged into the awaited `_disposeEngines` — only the timer loop is the missed dedup.)

```dart

final widgetLoader = _unpackedLoader(manager, store, loader);

```

Verified both constructors are pure field initializers (`UnpackedWidgetLoader` ctor: `appsStore = appsStore ?? AppsStore(env)`; `AppsStore` ctor assigns platform/readAsset only), so there is no observable behavior change — but the evaluation order did technically change.

### Observation (not a finding) — unpacked_load_flow.dart
The eager `_unpackedStore` also fixes a latent double-construction asymmetry: old code built `AppsStore(manager.env)` once; new code builds it once and passes it to the loader, identical to old. Injection precedence `loader?.appsStore ?? appsStore ?? AppsStore(...)` is byte-identical to old.

# PR #1881 review — UI widgets + network cluster (9 files)

Method: no shell available, so diffs were reconstructed by reading full NEW files locally and full OLD files fetched from raw.githubusercontent.com at merge-base 59fb4482ce (repo: IstiN/flutter_agent_harness). Verified per file: statement order, loop boundaries, short-circuit/early-return conditions, error paths/strings, closure captures, mutable-state threading, dropped/duplicated statements, defaults, string formatting. No `part`/`part of` splits were introduced in this cluster — all extractions are in-place private helpers, so no registration gaps possible.

## Findings

- **SUGGESTION** — `flutter_app/lib/ui/widgets/apps_panel.dart` ~line 183 (`_calendarReady(calendar)`) and ~line 190 (`_fetchUpcomingEvents(calendar)`): both new helpers declare the `calendar` parameter with no type (implicit `dynamic`). Old code inferred the concrete type from `createCalendarService()` at the use site. Compiles fine (flutter_app's analysis_options is plain `flutter_lints`, no `strict-inference`), but it defeats static checking on `calendar.isAvailable` / `calendar.events(...)` inside the extracted methods and deviates from the file's otherwise fully-typed style. Should be `CalendarApi calendar` (type is imported via `calendar_service.dart`).

## Detail checks the assignment called out

- **span_grid_delegate.dart `_packSpan`** — traced exhaustively, EQUIVALENT. Old inner structure: grow rows (`while (rows.length < cursorRow + h)`) → `fits = cursorCol + w <= crossAxisCount` → `dr`/`dc` scan with `&& fits` short-circuit → mark/add/`cursorCol += w`/break → wrap `if (++cursorCol + w > crossAxisCount) { cursorRow++; cursorCol = 0; }`. New: `_growRows` at the same point in the `while(true)`; `_spanFits` does `if (col + w > crossAxisCount) return false;` (exact negation of the old fits initializer, evaluated before the scan, so the case where `cursorCol` advanced past the row end behaves identically — old loop body ran zero iterations in that case too) then `_rowSegmentOccupied` (same `dc` scan, returns on first occupied, same short-circuit). Row indexing safe: `_growRows` guarantees `rows.length >= cursorRow + h` before `_spanFits` touches `rows[row + dr]`. Wrap condition byte-identical; success path returns `(cursorRow, cursorCol + w)` which the caller destructures — matches old `cursorCol += w; break`. No off-by-one, no infinite-loop change (cursor advancement identical on both paths). `w`/`h` clamping identical.
- **quick_switcher.dart** — contains no fuzzy matching; the recents logic (`_recentNetworkIds`, `i < recents.length && i < 7`, `_digitKeys[i + 3]!`) is untouched. The `_switchTo` change collapses three typed catches into one `on Object` + `_resumeErrorMessage` mapping: StateError→`e.message`, FaNetworkException→`e.message`, else→`'$e'` — same dispatch (the two types are unrelated, so catch order in the old code is preserved by the if-order). `context.mounted` guard moved into `_showResumeError`, checked before every snack, same as old.
- **file_preview.dart** — no filter logic exists here; extension dispatch verified: stat→mounted→error→`_size` assign→size cap→read→mounted→error→image-ext sniff (`sniffsAsImage`)→audio→video→binary (`_looksBinary`)→utf8/truncate/`_richKindFor`. Order and all caps/defaults unchanged; image branch correctly converted from early-`return` to if/else (no fall-through added).
- **github_connect_sheet.dart** — error-path strings unchanged everywhere: PAT catch → `error.message` / `error.toString()`; scope failure → `context.l10n.githubTokenNoRepoScope`; device flow → `_deviceFlowFailed` (endpointDisabled switches to token tab, else plain error) / `_deviceFlowFailedGeneric` (`error.toString()`, `_deviceStatus = null`) — bodies byte-identical to the old inline catches. The l10n closure in `_tokenConnectFailed(() => context.l10n...)` is invoked only under the `mounted` guard inside setState, matching the old `if (mounted)` blocks.

# Apps-cluster review — PR #1881 (chore/1848-crap-app-tier4)

Method: per-file patches from the GitHub PR files API (base 59fb4482ce → HEAD dcc6dcff81), cross-checked against full old files (raw.githubusercontent @59fb4482ce) and full new local files. No `part` files involved in this cluster — all extractions are private helpers in the same library, so no part-registration checks apply.

## Findings

### SUGGESTION — dynamic_messages.dart:640 — false doc claim / missed dedup
New code (line ~640):
```dart
/// Cancels the no-UI widgets' timers and drops them (shared by
/// [forgetAll] and [dispose]).
void _cancelNoUiTimers() { ... }
```
But `dispose()` (line ~651) still carries its **own inline copy** of the timer-cancel loop (`for (final timer in _noUiTimers.values) { timer.cancel(); } _noUiTimers.clear();`) and was not touched by the PR (the only hunk is `forgetAll`). The doc comment "shared by [forgetAll] and [dispose]" is factually wrong, and the duplicate loop the extraction should have removed is still there. No behavior change — either fix the doc or make `dispose()` call the helper. (Note: `dispose()` also keeps its deliberately *unawaited* `engine.dispose()` loop, which must NOT be merged into the awaited `_disposeEngines` — only the timer loop is the missed dedup.)

### SUGGESTION — unpacked_load_flow.dart:37-42 — inert reordering of pure constructions
Old: `createFolderPicker()` ran first, and when it returned null the function returned **before** `AppsStore(manager.env)` / `UnpackedWidgetLoader(...)` were constructed. New:
```dart
final store = _unpackedStore(manager, appsStore, loader);
final widgetLoader = _unpackedLoader(manager, store, loader);
await _runUnpackedLoad(...); // createFolderPicker() + null-return inside
```
The fallback `AppsStore(manager.env)` and `UnpackedWidgetLoader(env:, appsStore:)` are now constructed even on the no-op host-can't-pick path. Verified both constructors are pure field initializers (`UnpackedWidgetLoader` ctor: `appsStore = appsStore ?? AppsStore(env)`; `AppsStore` ctor assigns platform/readAsset only), so there is no observable behavior change — but the evaluation order did technically change.

### Observation (not a finding) — unpacked_load_flow.dart

# PR #1881 review — UI screens cluster (12 files)

## Findings

### 1. BLOCKING — `flutter_app/lib/ui/screens/settings_flows.dart:133` (+ `settings.dart` build, ~line 873): stale-model note (and structurally the CORS note) no longer rendered for on-device providers

**Old** (`settings.dart` @ 59fb4482ce, `build()`):
```dart
if (!_showProviderListOnly) ...[
  if (_isOnDevice) _buildWebLlmFields(theme)
  else if (_isGemma) _buildGemmaFields(theme)
  else if (_isTransformersJs) _buildTransformersJsFields(theme)
  else ...[ /* key/model/url fields */ ],
  if (corsNote != null) ...[ /* CORS note row */ ],        // sibling of the if/else chain
  if (_staleModelNote != null) ...[ /* stale-model note row */ ],
],
```
**New** (`settings_flows.dart`):
```dart
Widget _buildProviderConfigFields(...) {
  if (_isOnDevice) return _buildWebLlmFields(theme);        // line 133 — early return
  if (_isGemma) return _buildGemmaFields(theme);
  if (_isTransformersJs) return _buildTransformersJsFields(theme);
  return _buildStandardFields(theme, selection, corsNote);  // notes only inside here
}

# PR #1881 review — UI screens cluster (12 files)

## Findings

### 1. BLOCKING — `flutter_app/lib/ui/screens/settings_flows.dart:133` (+ `settings.dart` build, ~line 873): stale-model note (and structurally the CORS note) no longer rendered for on-device providers

**Old** (`settings.dart` @ 59fb4482ce, `build()`):
```dart
if (!_showProviderListOnly) ...[
  if (_isOnDevice) _buildWebLlmFields(theme)
  else if (_isGemma) _buildGemmaFields(theme)
  else if (_isTransformersJs) _buildTransformersJsFields(theme)
  else ...[ /* key/model/url fields */ ],
  if (corsNote != null) ...[ /* CORS note row */ ],        // sibling of the if/else chain
  if (_staleModelNote != null) ...[ /* stale-model note row */ ],
],
```
**New** (`settings_flows.dart`):
```dart
Widget _buildProviderConfigFields(...) {
  if (_isOnDevice) return _buildWebLlmFields(theme);        // line 133 — early return
  if (_isGemma) return _buildGemmaFields(theme);
  if (_isTransformersJs) return _buildTransformersJsFields(theme);
  return _buildStandardFields(theme, selection, corsNote);  // notes only inside here
}
```
`_staleModelNote` is set **exclusively** by the on-device verify paths (`_verifyWebLlmCache`, `_verifyGemmaInstalled`, `_verifyTransformersJsCache` — "cached weights are stale", "N of M installed" warnings) and is reset to null by `_selectProvider`, so it can only be non-null while an on-device provider is selected. By hoisting the notes into `_buildStandardFields` (hosted-only), the extraction made that note unreachable — a real user-facing behavior change in a PR claiming zero behavior change (the note's state setter is now dead UI). The CORS note is structurally dropped the same way but is practically unaffected (`ProviderPreset.cors` returns null for webllm/gemma/transformersJs — verified in `packages/fa_ui/lib/src/providers/provider_preset.dart`). Fix: render `..._buildConfigNotes(theme, corsNote)` after `_buildProviderConfigFields(...)` in `settings.dart` build, as siblings, matching the old tree.

No other issues in the settings split: `_connectHosted` preserves statement order, `mounted` guards, analytics calls, and rememberKey timing; `_applyLastConnection` branch extractions are verbatim; no BuildContext-across-async-gap introduced (all `context.l10n` uses in the extension are pre-await/synchronous); public API (SettingsScreen/AgentSettingsForm/SetupScreen signatures) unchanged; `part 'settings_flows.dart'` registration intact; the `_formSetState` bridge correctly avoids invalid_use_of_protected_member.

- **SUGGESTION** — `flutter_app/lib/ui/widgets/apps_panel.dart` ~line 183 (`_calendarReady(calendar)`) and ~line 190 (`_fetchUpcomingEvents(calendar)`): both new helpers declare the `calendar` parameter with no type (implicit `dynamic`). Old code inferred the concrete type from `createCalendarService()` at the use site. Compiles fine (flutter_app's analysis_options is plain `flutter_lints`, no `strict-inference`), but it defeats static checking on `calendar.isAvailable` / `calendar.events(...)` inside the extracted methods and deviates from the file's otherwise fully-typed style. Should be `CalendarApi calendar` (type is imported via `calendar_service.dart`).

## Detail checks the assignment called out

- **span_grid_delegate.dart `_packSpan`** — traced exhaustively, EQUIVALENT. Old inner structure: grow rows (`while (rows.length < cursorRow + h)`) → `fits = cursorCol + w <= crossAxisCount` → `dr`/`dc` scan with `&& fits` short-circuit → mark/add/`cursorCol += w`/break → wrap `if (++cursorCol + w > crossAxisCount) { cursorRow++; cursorCol = 0; }`. New: `_growRows` at the same point in the `while(true)`; `_spanFits` does `if (col + w > crossAxisCount) return false;` (exact negation of the old fits initializer, evaluated before the scan, so the case where `cursorCol` advanced past the row end behaves identically — old loop body ran zero iterations in that case too) then `_rowSegmentOccupied` (same `dc` scan, returns on first occupied, same short-circuit). Wrap condition byte-identical; success path returns `(cursorRow, cursorCol + w)` which the caller destructures — matches old `cursorCol += w; break`. No off-by-one, no infinite-loop change (cursor advancement identical on both paths). `w`/`h` clamping identical.

# PR #1881 review — UI screens cluster (12 files)

## Findings

### 1. BLOCKING — `flutter_app/lib/ui/screens/settings_flows.dart:133` (+ `settings.dart` build, ~line 873): stale-model note (and structurally the CORS note) no longer rendered for on-device providers

**Old** (`settings.dart` @ 59fb4482ce, `build()`):
```dart
if (!_showProviderListOnly) ...[
  if (_isOnDevice) _buildWebLlmFields(theme)
  else if (_isGemma) _buildGemmaFields(theme)
  else if (_isTransformersJs) _buildTransformersJsFields(theme)
  else ...[ /* key/model/url fields */ ],
  if (corsNote != null) ...[ /* CORS note row */ ],        // sibling of the if/else chain
  if (_staleModelNote != null) ...[ /* stale-model note row */ ],
],
```
**New** (`settings_flows.dart`):
```dart
Widget _buildProviderConfigFields(...) {
  if (_isOnDevice) return _buildWebLlmFields(theme);        // line 133 — early return
  if (_isGemma) return _buildGemmaFields(theme);
  if (_isTransformersJs) return _buildTransformersJsFields(theme);
  return _buildStandardFields(theme, selection, corsNote);  // notes only inside here
}
```
`_staleModelNote` is set **exclusively** by the on-device verify paths (`_verifyWebLlmCache`, `_verifyGemmaInstalled`, `_verifyTransformersJsCache` — "cached weights are stale", "N of M installed" warnings) and is reset to null by `_selectProvider`, so it can only be non-null while an on-device provider is selected. By hoisting the notes into `_buildStandardFields` (hosted-only), the extraction made that note unreachable — a real user-facing behavior change in a PR claiming zero behavior change (the note's state setter is now dead UI). The CORS note is structurally dropped the same way but is practically unaffected (`ProviderPreset.cors` returns null for webllm/gemma/transformersJs — verified in `packages/fa_ui/lib/src/providers/provider_preset.dart`). Fix: render `..._buildConfigNotes(theme, corsNote)` after `_buildProviderConfigFields(...)` in `settings.dart` build, as siblings, matching the old tree.

No other issues in the settings split: `_connectHosted` preserves statement order, `mounted` guards, analytics calls, and rememberKey timing; `_applyLastConnection` branch extractions are verbatim; no BuildContext-across-async-gap introduced (all `context.l10n` uses in the extension are pre-await/synchronous); public API (SettingsScreen/AgentSettingsForm/SetupScreen signatures) unchanged; `part 'settings_flows.dart'` registration intact; the `_formSetState` bridge correctly avoids invalid_use_of_protected_member.

## Per-file verdicts

| File | Verdict |
|---|---|
| `main.dart` | CLEAN — `MyApp.build` split into `_themeListenable`/`_materialApp`/`_navigatorBuilder`/`_wrapScopes`(+core/model/preview); ListenableBuilder listenable, scope nesting order (FahTheme→packs/sessionKeys/onDevice→media/task→chatText/imagePreviews), and all `BootstrapScreen` args identical. |

## Findings

### SUGGESTION — dynamic_messages.dart:640 — false doc claim / missed dedup
New code (line ~640):
```dart
/// Cancels the no-UI widgets' timers and drops them (shared by
/// [forgetAll] and [dispose]).
void _cancelNoUiTimers() { ... }
```
But `dispose()` (line ~651) still carries its **own inline copy** of the timer-cancel loop (`for (final timer in _noUiTimers.values) { timer.cancel(); } _noUiTimers.clear();`) and was not touched by the PR (the only hunk is `forgetAll`). The doc comment "shared by [forgetAll] and [dispose]" is factually wrong, and the duplicate loop the extraction should have removed is still there. No behavior change — either fix the doc or make `dispose()` call the helper. (Note: `dispose()` also keeps its deliberately *unawaited* `engine.dispose()` loop, which must NOT be merged into the awaited `_disposeEngines` — only the timer loop is the missed dedup.)

### SUGGESTION — unpacked_load_flow.dart:37-42 — inert reordering of pure constructions
Old: `createFolderPicker()` ran first, and when it returned null the function returned **before** `AppsStore(manager.env)` / `UnpackedWidgetLoader(...)` were constructed. New:
```dart
final store = _unpackedStore(manager, appsStore, loader);
final widgetLoader = _unpackedLoader(manager, store, loader);
await _runUnpackedLoad(...); // createFolderPicker() + null-return inside
```
The fallback `AppsStore(manager.env)` and `UnpackedWidgetLoader(env:, appsStore:)` are now constructed even on the no-op host-can't-pick path. Verified both constructors are pure field initializers (`UnpackedWidgetLoader` ctor: `appsStore = appsStore ?? AppsStore(env)`; `AppsStore` ctor assigns platform/readAsset only), so there is no observable behavior change — but the evaluation order did technically change.

### Observation (not a finding) — unpacked_load_flow.dart
The eager `_unpackedStore` also fixes a latent double-construction asymmetry: old code built `AppsStore(manager.env)` once; new code builds it once and passes it to the loader, identical to old. Injection precedence `loader?.appsStore ?? appsStore ?? AppsStore(...)` is byte-identical to old.

## File-by-file verification (all semantically identical unless noted above)

- **app_preflight_probe_io.dart — CLEAN.** `_probeJsEngineLibrary()` is called inside the same `try` that held the platform branch; `Platform.isMacOS || Platform.isIOS` evaluated once at the same point; the `on ArgumentError` fallback open stays inside the per-call try in `_probeJavaScriptCore` (a throwing fallback still propagates to the outer `on Object` exactly as before — the fallback open lives in the catch clause in both versions); the outer `on Object` catch swallows exactly the same failure set (nothing new escapes, nothing new is swallowed). Only hunk in the file (+22/−6).
- **catalog_auto_update.dart — CLEAN.** The three passes run in the same order over the same `result.entries`; the shared mutable `updated` list accumulates in identical sequence (pass 1 in-entry order, pass 2 in-entry order, pass 3 skipping `updated.contains(entry.id)` exactly as before); the per-entry try/catch swallow moved into `_reinstallFromCatalog` covers exactly the same statements (download → install → add…

```dart
if (!_showProviderListOnly) ...[
  if (_isOnDevice) _buildWebLlmFields(theme)

],
```
**New** (`settings_flows.dart`):
```dart

  if (_isOnDevice) return _buildWebLlmFields(theme);        // line 133 — early return
  if (_isGemma) return _buildGemmaFields(theme);
  if (_isTransformersJs) return _buildTransformersJsFields(theme);

## Findings

### SUGGESTION — dynamic_messages.dart:640 — false doc claim / missed dedup
New code (line ~640):
```dart
/// Cancels the no-UI widgets' timers and drops them (shared by
/// [forgetAll] and [dispose]).
void _cancelNoUiTimers() { ... }
```
But `dispose()` (line ~651) still carries its **own inline copy** of the timer-cancel loop (`for (final timer in _noUiTimers.values) { timer.cancel(); } _noUiTimers.clear();`) and was not touched by the PR (the only hunk is `forgetAll`). The doc comment "shared by [forgetAll] and [dispose]" is factually wrong, and the duplicate loop the extraction should have removed is still there. No behavior change — either fix the doc or make `dispose()` call the helper. (Note: `dispose()` also keeps its deliberately *unawaited* `engine.dispose()` loop, which must NOT be merged into the awaited `_disposeEngines` — only the timer loop is the missed dedup.)

### SUGGESTION — unpacked_load_flow.dart:37-42 — inert reordering of pure constructions
Old: `createFolderPicker()` ran first, and when it returned null the function returned **before** `AppsStore(manager.env)` / `UnpackedWidgetLoader(...)` were constructed. New:
```dart
final store = _unpackedStore(manager, appsStore, loader);
final widgetLoader = _unpackedLoader(manager, store, loader);
await _runUnpackedLoad(...); // createFolderPicker() + null-return inside
```
The fallback `AppsStore(manager.env)` and `UnpackedWidgetLoader(env:, appsStore:)` are now constructed even on the no-op host-can't-pick path. Verified both constructors are pure field initializers (`UnpackedWidgetLoader` ctor: `appsStore = appsStore ?? AppsStore(env)`; `AppsStore` ctor assigns platform/readAsset only), so there is no observable behavior change — but the evaluation order did technically change.

### Observation (not a finding) — unpacked_load_flow.dart
The eager `_unpackedStore` also fixes a latent double-construction asymmetry: old code built `AppsStore(manager.env)` once; new code builds it once and passes it to the loader, identical to old. Injection precedence `loader?.appsStore ?? appsStore ?? AppsStore(...)` is byte-identical to old.

- **catalog_auto_update.dart — CLEAN.** The three passes run in the same order over the same `result.entries`; the shared mutable `updated` list accumulates in identical sequence (pass 1 in-entry order, pass 2 in-entry order, pass 3 skipping `updated.contains(entry.id)` exactly as before); the per-entry try/catch swallow moved into `_reinstallFromCatalog` covers exactly the same statements (download → install → add…

**Old** (`settings.dart` @ 59fb4482ce, `build()`):
```dart
if (!_showProviderListOnly) ...[
  if (_isOnDevice) _buildWebLlmFields(theme)

],
```
**New** (`settings_flows.dart`):
```dart

  if (_isOnDevice) return _buildWebLlmFields(theme);        // line 133 — early return
  if (_isGemma) return _buildGemmaFields(theme);
  if (_isTransformersJs) return _buildTransformersJsFields(theme);

# PR #1881 review — UI screens cluster (12 files)

## Findings

### 1. BLOCKING — `flutter_app/lib/ui/screens/settings_flows.dart:133` (+ `settings.dart` build, ~line 873): stale-model note (and structurally the CORS note) no longer rendered for on-device providers

**Old** (`settings.dart` @ 59fb4482ce, `build()`):
```dart
if (!_showProviderListOnly) ...[
  if (_isOnDevice) _buildWebLlmFields(theme)
  else if (_isGemma) _buildGemmaFields(theme)
  else if (_isTransformersJs) _buildTransformersJsFields(theme)
  else ...[ /* key/model/url fields */ ],
  if (corsNote != null) ...[ /* CORS note row */ ],        // sibling of the if/else chain
  if (_staleModelNote != null) ...[ /* stale-model note row */ ],
],
```
**New** (`settings_flows.dart`):
```dart
Widget _buildProviderConfigFields(...) {
  if (_isOnDevice) return _buildWebLlmFields(theme);        // line 133 — early return
  if (_isGemma) return _buildGemmaFields(theme);
  if (_isTransformersJs) return _buildTransformersJsFields(theme);
  return _buildStandardFields(theme, selection, corsNote);  // notes only inside here
}
```
`_staleModelNote` is set **exclusively** by the on-device verify paths (`_verifyWebLlmCache`, `_verifyGemmaInstalled`, `_verifyTransformersJsCache` — "cached weights are stale", "N of M installed" warnings) and is reset to null by `_selectProvider`, so it can only be non-null while an on-device provider is selected. By hoisting the notes into `_buildStandardFields` (hosted-only), the extraction made that note unreachable — a real user-facing behavior change in a PR claiming zero behavior change (the note's state setter is now dead UI). # Apps-cluster review — PR #1881 (chore/1848-crap-app-tier4)

Method: per-file patches from the GitHub PR files API (base 59fb4482ce → HEAD dcc6dcff81), cross-checked against full old files (raw.githubusercontent @59fb4482ce) and full new local files. No `part` files involved in this cluster — all extractions are private helpers in the same library, so no part-registration checks apply.

## Findings

### SUGGESTION — dynamic_messages.dart:640 — false doc claim / missed dedup
New code (line ~640):
```dart
/// Cancels the no-UI widgets' timers and drops them (shared by
/// [forgetAll] and [dispose]).
void _cancelNoUiTimers() { ... }
```
But `dispose()` (line ~651) still carries its **own inline copy** of the timer-cancel loop (`for (final timer in _noUiTimers.values) { timer.cancel(); } _noUiTimers.clear();`) and was not touched by the PR (the only hunk is `forgetAll`). The doc comment "shared by [forgetAll] and [dispose]" is factually wrong, and the duplicate loop the extraction should have removed is still there. No behavior change — either fix the doc or make `dispose()` call the helper. (Note: `dispose()` also keeps its deliberately *unawaited* `engine.dispose()` loop, which must NOT be merged into the awaited `_disposeEngines` — only the timer loop is the missed dedup.)

### SUGGESTION — unpacked_load_flow.dart:37-42 — inert reordering of pure constructions
Old: `createFolderPicker()` ran first, and when it returned null the function returned **before** `AppsStore(manager.env)` / `UnpackedWidgetLoader(...)` were constructed. New:
```dart
final store = _unpackedStore(manager, appsStore, loader);
final widgetLoader = _unpackedLoader(manager, store, loader);
await _runUnpackedLoad(...); // createFolderPicker() + null-return inside
```
The fallback `AppsStore(manager.env)` and `UnpackedWidgetLoader(env:, appsStore:)` are now constructed even on the no-op host-can't-pick path. Verified both constructors are pure field initializers (`UnpackedWidgetLoader` ctor: `appsStore = appsStore ?? AppsStore(env)`; `AppsStore` ctor assigns platform/readAsset only), so there is no observable behavior change — but the evaluation order did technically change.

### Observation (not a finding) — unpacked_load_flow.dart

# PR #1881 review — UI screens cluster (12 files)

## Findings

### 1. BLOCKING — `flutter_app/lib/ui/screens/settings_flows.dart:133` (+ `settings.dart` build, ~line 873): stale-model note (and structurally the CORS note) no longer rendered for on-device providers

**Old** (`settings.dart` @ 59fb4482ce, `build()`):
```dart
if (!_showProviderListOnly) ...[
  if (_isOnDevice) _buildWebLlmFields(theme)
  else if (_isGemma) _buildGemmaFields(theme)
  else if (_isTransformersJs) _buildTransformersJsFields(theme)
  else ...[ /* key/model/url fields */ ],
  if (corsNote != null) ...[ /* CORS note row */ ],        // sibling of the if/else chain
  if (_staleModelNote != null) ...[ /* stale-model note row */ ],
],
```
**New** (`settings_flows.dart`):
```dart
Widget _buildProviderConfigFields(...) {
  if (_isOnDevice) return _buildWebLlmFields(theme);        // line 133 — early return
  if (_isGemma) return _buildGemmaFields(theme);
  if (_isTransformersJs) return _buildTransformersJsFields(theme);
  return _buildStandardFields(theme, selection, corsNote);  // notes only inside here
}

# PR #1881 review — UI screens cluster (12 files)

## Findings

### 1. BLOCKING — `flutter_app/lib/ui/screens/settings_flows.dart:133` (+ `settings.dart` build, ~line 873): stale-model note (and structurally the CORS note) no longer rendered for on-device providers

**Old** (`settings.dart` @ 59fb4482ce, `build()`):
```dart
if (!_showProviderListOnly) ...[
  if (_isOnDevice) _buildWebLlmFields(theme)
  else if (_isGemma) _buildGemmaFields(theme)
  else if (_isTransformersJs) _buildTransformersJsFields(theme)
  else ...[ /* key/model/url fields */ ],
  if (corsNote != null) ...[ /* CORS note row */ ],        // sibling of the if/else chain
  if (_staleModelNote != null) ...[ /* stale-model note row */ ],
],
```
**New** (`settings_flows.dart`):
```dart
Widget _buildProviderConfigFields(...) {
  if (_isOnDevice) return _buildWebLlmFields(theme);        // line 133 — early return
  if (_isGemma) return _buildGemmaFields(theme);
  if (_isTransformersJs) return _buildTransformersJsFields(theme);
  return _buildStandardFields(theme, selection, corsNote);  // notes only inside here
}
```
`_staleModelNote` is set **exclusively** by the on-device verify paths (`_verifyWebLlmCache`, `_verifyGemmaInstalled`, `_verifyTransformersJsCache` — "cached weights are stale", "N of M installed" warnings) and is reset to null by `_selectProvider`, so it can only be non-null while an on-device provider is selected. By hoisting the notes into `_buildStandardFields` (hosted-only), the extraction made that note unreachable — a real user-facing behavior change in a PR claiming zero behavior change (the note's state setter is now dead UI). The CORS note is structurally dropped the same way but is practically unaffected (`ProviderPreset.cors` returns null for webllm/gemma/transformersJs — verified in `packages/fa_ui/lib/src/providers/provider_preset.dart`). Fix: render `..._buildConfigNotes(theme, corsNote)` after `_buildProviderConfigFields(...)` in `settings.dart` build, as siblings, matching the old tree.

No other issues in the settings split: `_connectHosted` preserves statement order, `mounted` guards, analytics calls, and rememberKey timing; `_applyLastConnection` branch extractions are verbatim; no BuildContext-across-async-gap introduced (all `context.l10n` uses in the extension are pre-await/synchronous); public API (SettingsScreen/AgentSettingsForm/SetupScreen signatures) unchanged; `part 'settings_flows.dart'` registration intact; the `_formSetState` bridge correctly avoids invalid_use_of_protected_member.

- **SUGGESTION** — `flutter_app/lib/ui/widgets/apps_panel.dart` ~line 183 (`_calendarReady(calendar)`) and ~line 190 (`_fetchUpcomingEvents(calendar)`): both new helpers declare the `calendar` parameter with no type (implicit `dynamic`). Old code inferred the concrete type from `createCalendarService()` at the use site. Compiles fine (flutter_app's analysis_options is plain `flutter_lints`, no `strict-inference`), but it defeats static checking on `calendar.isAvailable` / `calendar.events(...)` inside the extracted methods and deviates from the file's otherwise fully-typed style. Should be `CalendarApi calendar` (type is imported via `calendar_service.dart`).

## Detail checks the assignment called out

- **span_grid_delegate.dart `_packSpan`** — traced exhaustively, EQUIVALENT. Old inner structure: grow rows (`while (rows.length < cursorRow + h)`) → `fits = cursorCol + w <= crossAxisCount` → `dr`/`dc` scan with `&& fits` short-circuit → mark/add/`cursorCol += w`/break → wrap `if (++cursorCol + w > crossAxisCount) { cursorRow++; cursorCol = 0; }`. New: `_growRows` at the same point in the `while(true)`; `_spanFits` does `if (col + w > crossAxisCount) return false;` (exact negation of the old fits initializer, evaluated before the scan, so the case where `cursorCol` advanced past the row end behaves identically — old loop body ran zero iterations in that case too) then `_rowSegmentOccupied` (same `dc` scan, returns on first occupied, same short-circuit).
