Wrap condition byte-identical; success path returns `(cursorRow, cursorCol + w)` which the caller destructures — matches old `cursorCol += w; break`. No off-by-one, no infinite-loop change (cursor advancement identical on both paths). `w`/`h` clamping identical.

# Apps-cluster review — PR #1881 (chore/1848-crap-app-tier4)

Method: per-file patches from the GitHub PR files API (base 59fb4482ce → HEAD dcc6dcff81), cross-checked against full old files (raw.githubusercontent @59fb4482ce) and full new local files. No `part` files involved in this cluster — all extractions are private helpers in the same library, so no part-registration checks apply.

## Findings

### SUGGESTION — dynamic_messages.dart:640 — false doc claim / missed dedup
New code (line ~640):
```dart
/// Cancels the no-UI widgets' timers and drops them (shared by
/// [forgetAll] and [dispose]).
void _cancelNoUiTimers() { ... }
```
But `dispose()` (line ~651) still carries its **own inline copy** of the timer-cancel loop (`for (final timer in _noUiTimers.values) { timer.cancel(); } _noUiTimers.clear();`) and was not touched by the PR (the only hunk is `forgetAll`). The doc comment "shared by [forgetAll] and [dispose]" is factually wrong, and the duplicate loop the extraction should have removed is still there. No behavior change — either fix the doc or make `dispose()` call the helper. (Note: `dispose()` also keeps its deliberately *unawaited* `engine.dispose()` loop, which must NOT be merged into the awaited `_disposeEngines` — only the timer loop is the missed dedup.)

### SUGGESTION — unpacked_load_flow.dart:37-42 — inert reordering of pure constructions
Old: `createFolderPicker()` ran first, and when it returned null the function returned **before** `AppsStore(manager.env)` / `UnpackedWidgetLoader(...)` were constructed. New:
```dart
final store = _unpackedStore(manager, appsStore, loader);
final widgetLoader = _unpackedLoader(manager, store, loader);
await _runUnpackedLoad(...); // createFolderPicker() + null-return inside
```
The fallback `AppsStore(manager.env)` and `UnpackedWidgetLoader(env:, appsStore:)` are now constructed even on the no-op host-can't-pick path. Verified both constructors are pure field initializers (`UnpackedWidgetLoader` ctor: `appsStore = appsStore ?? AppsStore(env)`; `AppsStore` ctor assigns platform/readAsset only), so there is no observable behavior change — but the evaluation order did technically change.

### Observation (not a finding) — unpacked_load_flow.dart
The eager `_unpackedStore` also fixes a latent double-construction asymmetry: old code built `AppsStore(manager.env)` once; new code builds it once and passes it to the loader, identical to old. Injection precedence `loader?.appsStore ?? appsStore ?? AppsStore(...)` is byte-identical to old.

## File-by-file verification (all semantically identical unless noted above)

- **app_preflight_probe_io.dart — CLEAN.** `_probeJsEngineLibrary()` is called inside the same `try` that held the platform branch; `Platform.isMacOS || Platform.isIOS` evaluated once at the same point; the `on ArgumentError` fallback open stays inside the per-call try in `_probeJavaScriptCore` (a throwing fallback still propagates to the outer `on Object` exactly as before — the fallback open lives in the catch clause in both versions); the outer `on Object` catch swallows exactly the same failure set (nothing new escapes, nothing new is swallowed). QuickJS env-var fallback chain unchanged.
- **apps_store.dart — CLEAN.** `_i18nRefsUnchanged` → `_allI18nRefsUnchanged` + `_i18nRefUnchanged`: same `recorded.entries` iteration order, same first-changed short-circuit, same read+digest comparison (`current != null && _digest(current) == entry.value` ≡ `!(current == null || digest != value)`), `recorded == null → true` preserved. Only hunk in the file (+22/−6).
- **catalog_auto_update.dart — CLEAN.** The three passes run in the same order over the same `result.entries`; the shared mutable `updated` list accumulates in identical sequence (pass 1 in-entry order, pass 2 in-entry order, pass 3 skipping `updated.contains(entry.id)` exactly as before); the per-entry try/catch swallow moved into `_reinstallFromCatalog` covers exactly the same statements (download → install → add…

# PR #1881 review — UI screens cluster (12 files)

## Findings

### 1. BLOCKING — `flutter_app/lib/ui/screens/settings_flows.dart:133` (+ `settings.dart` build, ~line 873): stale-model note (and structurally the CORS note) no longer rendered for on-device providers

**Old** (`settings.dart` @ 59fb4482ce, `build()`):
```dart
if (!_showProviderListOnly) ...[
  if (_isOnDevice) _buildWebLlmFields(theme)
  else if (_isGemma) _buildGemmaFields(theme)
  else if (_isTransformersJs) _buildTransformersJsFields(theme)
  else ...[ /* key/model/url fields */ ],
  if (corsNote != null) ...[ /* CORS note row */ ],        // sibling of the if/else chain
  if (_staleModelNote != null) ...[ /* stale-model note row */ ],
],
```
**New** (`settings_flows.dart`):
```dart
Widget _buildProviderConfigFields(...) {
  if (_isOnDevice) return _buildWebLlmFields(theme);        // line 133 — early return
  if (_isGemma) return _buildGemmaFields(theme);
  if (_isTransformersJs) return _buildTransformersJsFields(theme);
  return _buildStandardFields(theme, selection, corsNote);  // notes only inside here
}
```

# PR #1881 review — UI screens cluster (12 files)

## Findings

### 1. BLOCKING — `flutter_app/lib/ui/screens/settings_flows.dart:133` (+ `settings.dart` build, ~line 873): stale-model note (and structurally the CORS note) no longer rendered for on-device providers

**Old** (`settings.dart` @ 59fb4482ce, `build()`):
```dart
if (!_showProviderListOnly) ...[
  if (_isOnDevice) _buildWebLlmFields(theme)
  else if (_isGemma) _buildGemmaFields(theme)
  else if (_isTransformersJs) _buildTransformersJsFields(theme)
  else ...[ /* key/model/url fields */ ],
  if (corsNote != null) ...[ /* CORS note row */ ],        // sibling of the if/else chain
  if (_staleModelNote != null) ...[ /* stale-model note row */ ],
],
```
**New** (`settings_flows.dart`):
```dart
Widget _buildProviderConfigFields(...) {
  if (_isOnDevice) return _buildWebLlmFields(theme);        // line 133 — early return
  if (_isGemma) return _buildGemmaFields(theme);
  if (_isTransformersJs) return _buildTransformersJsFields(theme);
  return _buildStandardFields(theme, selection, corsNote);  // notes only inside here
}
```
`_staleModelNote` is set **exclusively** by the on-device verify paths (`_verifyWebLlmCache`, `_verifyGemmaInstalled`, `_verifyTransformersJsCache` — "cached weights are stale", "N of M installed" warnings) and is reset to null by `_selectProvider`, so it can only be non-null while an on-device provider is selected. By hoisting the notes into `_buildStandardFields` (hosted-only), the extraction made that note unreachable — a real user-facing behavior change in a PR claiming zero behavior change (the note's state setter is now dead UI). The CORS note is structurally dropped the same way but is practically unaffected (`ProviderPreset.cors` returns null for webllm/gemma/transformersJs — verified in `packages/fa_ui/lib/src/providers/provider_preset.dart`). Fix: render `..._buildConfigNotes(theme, corsNote)` after `_buildProviderConfigFields(...)` in `settings.dart` build, as siblings, matching the old tree.

# PR #1881 review — UI screens cluster (12 files)

## Findings

### 1. BLOCKING — `flutter_app/lib/ui/screens/settings_flows.dart:133` (+ `settings.dart` build, ~line 873): stale-model note (and structurally the CORS note) no longer rendered for on-device providers

**Old** (`settings.dart` @ 59fb4482ce, `build()`):
```dart
if (!_showProviderListOnly) ...[
  if (_isOnDevice) _buildWebLlmFields(theme)
  else if (_isGemma) _buildGemmaFields(theme)
  else if (_isTransformersJs) _buildTransformersJsFields(theme)
  else ...[ /* key/model/url fields */ ],
  if (corsNote != null) ...[ /* CORS note row */ ],        // sibling of the if/else chain
  if (_staleModelNote != null) ...[ /* stale-model note row */ ],
],
```
**New** (`settings_flows.dart`):
```dart
Widget _buildProviderConfigFields(...) {
  if (_isOnDevice) return _buildWebLlmFields(theme);        // line 133 — early return
  if (_isGemma) return _buildGemmaFields(theme);
  if (_isTransformersJs) return _buildTransformersJsFields(theme);
  return _buildStandardFields(theme, selection, corsNote);  // notes only inside here
}
```

**Old** (`settings.dart` @ 59fb4482ce, `build()`):
```dart
if (!_showProviderListOnly) ...[
  if (_isOnDevice) _buildWebLlmFields(theme)

],
```
**New** (`settings_flows.dart`):
```dart

  if (_isOnDevice) return _buildWebLlmFields(theme);        // line 133 — early return
  if (_isGemma) return _buildGemmaFields(theme);
  if (_isTransformersJs) return _buildTransformersJsFields(theme);
```

# PR #1881 review — UI screens cluster (12 files)

## Findings

### 1. BLOCKING — `flutter_app/lib/ui/screens/settings_flows.dart:133` (+ `settings.dart` build, ~line 873): stale-model note (and structurally the CORS note) no longer rendered for on-device providers

**Old** (`settings.dart` @ 59fb4482ce, `build()`):
```dart
if (!_showProviderListOnly) ...[
  if (_isOnDevice) _buildWebLlmFields(theme)
  else if (_isGemma) _buildGemmaFields(theme)
  else if (_isTransformersJs) _buildTransformersJsFields(theme)
  else ...[ /* key/model/url fields */ ],
  if (corsNote != null) ...[ /* CORS note row */ ],        // sibling of the if/else chain
  if (_staleModelNote != null) ...[ /* stale-model note row */ ],
],
```
**New** (`settings_flows.dart`):
```dart
Widget _buildProviderConfigFields(...) {
  if (_isOnDevice) return _buildWebLlmFields(theme);        // line 133 — early return
  if (_isGemma) return _buildGemmaFields(theme);
  if (_isTransformersJs) return _buildTransformersJsFields(theme);
  return _buildStandardFields(theme, selection, corsNote);  // notes only inside here
}
```
`_staleModelNote` is set **exclusively** by the on-device verify paths (`_verifyWebLlmCache`, `_verifyGemmaInstalled`, `_verifyTransformersJsCache` — "cached weights are stale", "N of M installed" warnings) and is reset to null by `_selectProvider`, so it can only be non-null while an on-device provider is selected. By hoisting the notes into `_buildStandardFields` (hosted-only), the extraction made that note unreachable — a real user-facing behavior change in a PR claiming zero behavior change (the note's state setter is now dead UI). Fix: render `..._buildConfigNotes(theme, corsNote)` after `_buildProviderConfigFields(...)` in `settings.dart` build, as siblings, matching the old tree.

```dart
/// Cancels the no-UI widgets' timers and drops them (shared by

void _cancelNoUiTimers() { ... }
```
But `dispose()` (line ~651) still carries its **own inline copy** of the timer-cancel loop (`for (final timer in _noUiTimers.values) { timer.cancel(); } _noUiTimers.clear();`) and was not touched by the PR (the only hunk is `forgetAll`). final store = _unpackedStore(manager, appsStore, loader);

```dart
await _runUnpackedLoad(...); // createFolderPicker() + null-return inside
```
The fallback `AppsStore(manager.env)` and `UnpackedWidgetLoader(env:, appsStore:)` are now constructed even on the no-op host-can't-pick path. Verified both constructors are pure field initializers (`UnpackedWidgetLoader` ctor: `appsStore = appsStore ?? AppsStore(env)`; `AppsStore` ctor assigns platform/readAsset only), so there is no observable behavior change — but the evaluation order did technically change.

### Observation (not a finding) — unpacked_load_flow.dart
The eager `_unpackedStore` also fixes a latent double-construction asymmetry: old code built `AppsStore(manager.env)` once; new code builds it once and passes it to the loader, identical to old. Injection precedence `loader?.appsStore ?? appsStore ?? AppsStore(...)` is byte-identical to old.

### 1. SUGGESTION — `flutter_app/lib/services/relay_agent_service.dart:954` — `mail_routed` now notifies listeners once instead of twice

**Old** (`_onHostEvent` switch, base 59fb4482ce): the `mail_routed` case called `if (!silent) notifyListeners();` inside the case (the "Paint NOW" comment), and then the trailing `if (!silent) notifyListeners();` after the switch fired for ALL event types — so `mail_routed` notified **twice** when live.
**New**: `_onHostMailRoutedEvent` (lines 944–955) contains exactly one `if (!silent) notifyListeners();`, and its caller `_onHostStateEvent` does not notify after the `mail_routed` arm (only the `tool_result`/`status` arm via `_onHostProgressEvent` and the default arm via `_onHostDiagnosticsEvent` notify, once each). All other event types keep the identical single notify; only `mail_routed` changes (2 → 1 `notifyListeners()`). The double-notify was almost certainly an accident, so the new code is arguably a fix — but it is a literal behavior deviation in a "zero behavior change" PR and should get a one-line callout in the PR description. # PR #1881 review — UI screens cluster (12 files)

## Findings

### 1. BLOCKING — `flutter_app/lib/ui/screens/settings_flows.dart:133` (+ `settings.dart` build, ~line 873): stale-model note (and structurally the CORS note) no longer rendered for on-device providers

**Old** (`settings.dart` @ 59fb4482ce, `build()`):
```dart
if (!_showProviderListOnly) ...[
  if (_isOnDevice) _buildWebLlmFields(theme)
  else if (_isGemma) _buildGemmaFields(theme)
  else if (_isTransformersJs) _buildTransformersJsFields(theme)
  else ...[ /* key/model/url fields */ ],
  if (corsNote != null) ...[ /* CORS note row */ ],        // sibling of the if/else chain
  if (_staleModelNote != null) ...[ /* stale-model note row */ ],
],
```
**New** (`settings_flows.dart`):
```dart
Widget _buildProviderConfigFields(...) {
  if (_isOnDevice) return _buildWebLlmFields(theme);        // line 133 — early return
  if (_isGemma) return _buildGemmaFields(theme);
  if (_isTransformersJs) return _buildTransformersJsFields(theme);
  return _buildStandardFields(theme, selection, corsNote);  // notes only inside here
}
```

# PR #1881 review — UI screens cluster (12 files)

## Findings

### 1. BLOCKING — `flutter_app/lib/ui/screens/settings_flows.dart:133` (+ `settings.dart` build, ~line 873): stale-model note (and structurally the CORS note) no longer rendered for on-device providers

**Old** (`settings.dart` @ 59fb4482ce, `build()`):
```dart
if (!_showProviderListOnly) ...[
  if (_isOnDevice) _buildWebLlmFields(theme)
  else if (_isGemma) _buildGemmaFields(theme)
  else if (_isTransformersJs) _buildTransformersJsFields(theme)
  else ...[ /* key/model/url fields */ ],
  if (corsNote != null) ...[ /* CORS note row */ ],        // sibling of the if/else chain
  if (_staleModelNote != null) ...[ /* stale-model note row */ ],
],
```
**New** (`settings_flows.dart`):
```dart
Widget _buildProviderConfigFields(...) {
  if (_isOnDevice) return _buildWebLlmFields(theme);        // line 133 — early return
  if (_isGemma) return _buildGemmaFields(theme);
  if (_isTransformersJs) return _buildTransformersJsFields(theme);
  return _buildStandardFields(theme, selection, corsNote);  // notes only inside here
}
```
`_staleModelNote` is set **exclusively** by the on-device verify paths (`_verifyWebLlmCache`, `_verifyGemmaInstalled`, `_verifyTransformersJsCache` — "cached weights are stale", "N of M installed" warnings) and is reset to null by `_selectProvider`, so it can only be non-null while an on-device provider is selected. By hoisting the notes into `_buildStandardFields` (hosted-only), the extraction made that note unreachable — a real user-facing behavior change in a PR claiming zero behavior change (the note's state setter is now dead UI). The CORS note is structurally dropped the same way but is practically unaffected (`ProviderPreset.cors` returns null for webllm/gemma/transformersJs — verified in `packages/fa_ui/lib/src/providers/provider_preset.dart`). Fix: render `..._buildConfigNotes(theme, corsNote)` after `_buildProviderConfigFields(...)` in `settings.dart` build, as siblings, matching the old tree.

No other issues in the settings split: `_connectHosted` preserves statement order, `mounted` guards, analytics calls, and rememberKey timing; `_applyLastConnection` branch extractions are verbatim; no BuildContext-across-async-gap introduced (all `context.l10n` uses in the extension are pre-await/synchronous); public API (SettingsScreen/AgentSettingsForm/SetupScreen signatures) unchanged; `part 'settings_flows.dart'` registration intact; the `_formSetState` bridge correctly avoids invalid_use_of_protected_member.

# PR #1881 review — UI screens cluster (12 files)

## Findings

### 1. BLOCKING — `flutter_app/lib/ui/screens/settings_flows.dart:133` (+ `settings.dart` build, ~line 873): stale-model note (and structurally the CORS note) no longer rendered for on-device providers

**Old** (`settings.dart` @ 59fb4482ce, `build()`):
```dart
if (!_showProviderListOnly) ...[
  if (_isOnDevice) _buildWebLlmFields(theme)
  else if (_isGemma) _buildGemmaFields(theme)
  else if (_isTransformersJs) _buildTransformersJsFields(theme)
  else ...[ /* key/model/url fields */ ],
  if (corsNote != null) ...[ /* CORS note row */ ],        // sibling of the if/else chain
  if (_staleModelNote != null) ...[ /* stale-model note row */ ],
],
```
**New** (`settings_flows.dart`):
```dart
Widget _buildProviderConfigFields(...) {
  if (_isOnDevice) return _buildWebLlmFields(theme);        // line 133 — early return
  if (_isGemma) return _buildGemmaFields(theme);
  if (_isTransformersJs) return _buildTransformersJsFields(theme);
  return _buildStandardFields(theme, selection, corsNote);  // notes only inside here
}
```
`_staleModelNote` is set **exclusively** by the on-device verify paths (`_verifyWebLlmCache`, `_verifyGemmaInstalled`, `_verifyTransformersJsCache` — "cached weights are stale", "N of M installed" warnings) and is reset to null by `_selectProvider`, so it can only be non-null while an on-device provider is selected. Old code inferred the concrete type from `createCalendarService()` at the use site. Compiles fine (flutter_app's analysis_options is plain `flutter_lints`, no `strict-inference`), but it defeats static checking on `calendar.isAvailable` / `calendar.events(...)` inside the extracted methods and deviates from the file's otherwise fully-typed style. Wrap condition byte-identical; success path returns `(cursorRow, cursorCol + w)` which the caller destructures — matches old `cursorCol += w; break`. # PR #1881 review — UI screens cluster (12 files)

## Findings

### 1. BLOCKING — `flutter_app/lib/ui/screens/settings_flows.dart:133` (+ `settings.dart` build, ~line 873): stale-model note (and structurally the CORS note) no longer rendered for on-device providers

**Old** (`settings.dart` @ 59fb4482ce, `build()`):
```dart
if (!_showProviderListOnly) ...[
  if (_isOnDevice) _buildWebLlmFields(theme)
  else if (_isGemma) _buildGemmaFields(theme)
  else if (_isTransformersJs) _buildTransformersJsFields(theme)
  else ...[ /* key/model/url fields */ ],
  if (corsNote != null) ...[ /* CORS note row */ ],        // sibling of the if/else chain
  if (_staleModelNote != null) ...[ /* stale-model note row */ ],
],
```
**New** (`settings_flows.dart`):
```dart
Widget _buildProviderConfigFields(...) {
  if (_isOnDevice) return _buildWebLlmFields(theme);        // line 133 — early return
  if (_isGemma) return _buildGemmaFields(theme);
  if (_isTransformersJs) return _buildTransformersJsFields(theme);
  return _buildStandardFields(theme, selection, corsNote);  // notes only inside here
}
```
`_staleModelNote` is set **exclusively** by the on-device verify paths (`_verifyWebLlmCache`, `_verifyGemmaInstalled`, `_verifyTransformersJsCache` — "cached weights are stale", "N of M installed" warnings) and is reset to null by `_selectProvider`, so it can only be non-null while an on-device provider is selected. By hoisting the notes into `_buildStandardFields` (hosted-only), the extraction made that note unreachable — a real user-facing behavior change in a PR claiming zero behavior change (the note's state setter is now dead UI). The CORS note is structurally dropped the same way but is practically unaffected (`ProviderPreset.cors` returns null for webllm/gemma/transformersJs — verified in `packages/fa_ui/lib/src/providers/provider_preset.dart`). Fix: render `..._buildConfigNotes(theme, corsNote)` after `_buildProviderConfigFields(...)` in `settings.dart` build, as siblings, matching the old tree.

The CORS half of the move is practically inert (`ProviderPreset.cors` is null for all three on-device presets), but the stale-model half is a genuine regression.

**Fix** (one line at the call site): render the notes as siblings again, as they were —

```dart
if (!_showProviderListOnly) ...[
  _buildProviderConfigFields(theme, selection, corsNote),
  ..._buildConfigNotes(theme, corsNote),
],
```

— and drop `..._buildConfigNotes(theme, corsNote)` from `_buildStandardFields` so it isn't duplicated on the hosted path.

💡 **SUGGESTION: untyped `calendar` parameter (implicit `dynamic`)**

Both new helpers declare the parameter untyped:

```dart
Future<bool> _calendarReady(calendar) async { ... }
Future<void> _fetchUpcomingEvents(calendar) async { ... }
```

The old inline code held the inferred concrete type (`final calendar = createCalendarService();`). The bare identifier defaults to `dynamic`, which compiles (no error even under this repo's strict lints) but weakens static checking and deviates from the surrounding style where every parameter carries a type. Please type them `CalendarService` (the `createCalendarService()` return type).

💡 **SUGGESTION: `mail_routed` now notifies once instead of twice**

Pre-split, a live `mail_routed` event fired `notifyListeners()` twice: once in the case body ("Paint NOW") and once from the unconditional trailing `if (!silent) notifyListeners();` at the end of `_onHostEvent`. After the split, `_onHostMailRoutedEvent` fires it once and `_onHostStateEvent` has no trailing notify.

The extra notification was redundant (listeners rebuild idempotently), so nothing user-visible changes — but it is a literal deviation from the PR's "zero behavior change" claim, and any listener counting notifications (tests, perf probes) would observe the difference. Worth a one-line mention in the PR description; no code change needed.

# PR #1881 review — UI screens cluster (12 files)

**Old** (`settings.dart` @ 59fb4482ce, `build()`):
```dart
if (!_showProviderListOnly) ...[
  if (_isOnDevice) _buildWebLlmFields(theme)
  else if (_isGemma) _buildGemmaFields(theme)
  else if (_isTransformersJs) _buildTransformersJsFields(theme)
  else ...[ /* key/model/url fields */ ],
  if (corsNote != null) ...[ /* CORS note row */ ],        // sibling of the if/else chain
  if (_staleModelNote != null) ...[ /* stale-model note row */ ],
],
```
**New** (`settings_flows.dart`):
```dart
Widget _buildProviderConfigFields(...) {
  if (_isOnDevice) return _buildWebLlmFields(theme);        // line 133 — early return
  if (_isGemma) return _buildGemmaFields(theme);
  if (_isTransformersJs) return _buildTransformersJsFields(theme);
  return _buildStandardFields(theme, selection, corsNote);  // notes only inside here
}
```

```dart
if (!_showProviderListOnly) ...[
  if (_isOnDevice) _buildWebLlmFields(theme)
```

```dart
  if (_isGemma) return _buildGemmaFields(theme);
  if (_isTransformersJs) return _buildTransformersJsFields(theme);
```

# Review: agent services cluster — PR #1881 (chore/1848-crap-app-tier4)

## Findings

### 1. SUGGESTION — `flutter_app/lib/services/relay_agent_service.dart:954` — `mail_routed` now notifies listeners once instead of twice

**Old** (`_onHostEvent` switch, base 59fb4482ce): the `mail_routed` case called `if (!silent) notifyListeners();` inside the case (the "Paint NOW" comment), and then the trailing `if (!silent) notifyListeners();` after the switch fired for ALL event types — so `mail_routed` notified **twice** when live.
**New**: `_onHostMailRoutedEvent` (lines 944–955) contains exactly one `if (!silent) notifyListeners();`, and its caller `_onHostStateEvent` does not notify after the `mail_routed` arm (only the `tool_result`/`status` arm via `_onHostProgressEvent` and the default arm via `_onHostDiagnosticsEvent` notify, once each). All other event types keep the identical single notify; only `mail_routed` changes (2 → 1 `notifyListeners()`). The double-notify was almost certainly an accident, so the new code is arguably a fix — but it is a literal behavior deviation in a "zero behavior change" PR and should get a one-line callout in the PR description. No rework needed.

## Verified clean (with the specific checks requested)

- **agent_service_events.dart route table** — `_agentEventHandlers` keys are exactly the old switch's 10 cases (AgentStart, TurnStart, MessageUpdate, MessageEnd, ToolExecutionStart, ToolExecutionEnd, ModelRequest, ToolPairingRepair, AgentEnd); unmapped kinds no-op like the old `default: break;`. # PR #1881 review — UI screens cluster (12 files)

## Findings

### 1. BLOCKING — `flutter_app/lib/ui/screens/settings_flows.dart:133` (+ `settings.dart` build, ~line 873): stale-model note (and structurally the CORS note) no longer rendered for on-device providers

**Old** (`settings.dart` @ 59fb4482ce, `build()`):
```dart
if (!_showProviderListOnly) ...[
  if (_isOnDevice) _buildWebLlmFields(theme)
  else if (_isGemma) _buildGemmaFields(theme)
  else if (_isTransformersJs) _buildTransformersJsFields(theme)

  if (_staleModelNote != null) ...[ /* stale-model note row */ ],
],
```
**New** (`settings_flows.dart`):
```dart
Widget _buildProviderConfigFields(...) {
  if (_isOnDevice) return _buildWebLlmFields(theme);        // line 133 — early return
  if (_isGemma) return _buildGemmaFields(theme);
  if (_isTransformersJs) return _buildTransformersJsFields(theme);
  return _buildStandardFields(theme, selection, corsNote);  // notes only inside here
```

# PR #1881 review — UI screens cluster (12 files)

## Findings

### 1. BLOCKING — `flutter_app/lib/ui/screens/settings_flows.dart:133` (+ `settings.dart` build, ~line 873): stale-model note (and structurally the CORS note) no longer rendered for on-device providers

**Old** (`settings.dart` @ 59fb4482ce, `build()`):
```dart
if (!_showProviderListOnly) ...[
  if (_isOnDevice) _buildWebLlmFields(theme)
  else if (_isGemma) _buildGemmaFields(theme)
  else if (_isTransformersJs) _buildTransformersJsFields(theme)
  else ...[ /* key/model/url fields */ ],
  if (corsNote != null) ...[ /* CORS note row */ ],        // sibling of the if/else chain
  if (_staleModelNote != null) ...[ /* stale-model note row */ ],
],
```
**New** (`settings_flows.dart`):
```dart
Widget _buildProviderConfigFields(...) {
  if (_isOnDevice) return _buildWebLlmFields(theme);        // line 133 — early return
  if (_isGemma) return _buildGemmaFields(theme);
  if (_isTransformersJs) return _buildTransformersJsFields(theme);
  return _buildStandardFields(theme, selection, corsNote);  // notes only inside here
}
```
`_staleModelNote` is set **exclusively** by the on-device verify paths (`_verifyWebLlmCache`, `_verifyGemmaInstalled`, `_verifyTransformersJsCache` — "cached weights are stale", "N of M installed" warnings) and is reset to null by `_selectProvider`, so it can only be non-null while an on-device provider is selected. Old code inferred the concrete type from `createCalendarService()` at the use site. Compiles fine (flutter_app's analysis_options is plain `flutter_lints`, no `strict-inference`), but it defeats static checking on `calendar.isAvailable` / `calendar.events(...)` inside the extracted methods and deviates from the file's otherwise fully-typed style. # PR #1881 review — UI screens cluster (12 files)

## Findings

### 1. BLOCKING — `flutter_app/lib/ui/screens/settings_flows.dart:133` (+ `settings.dart` build, ~line 873): stale-model note (and structurally the CORS note) no longer rendered for on-device providers

**Old** (`settings.dart` @ 59fb4482ce, `build()`):
```dart
if (!_showProviderListOnly) ...[
  if (_isOnDevice) _buildWebLlmFields(theme)
  else if (_isGemma) _buildGemmaFields(theme)
  else if (_isTransformersJs) _buildTransformersJsFields(theme)
  else ...[ /* key/model/url fields */ ],
  if (corsNote != null) ...[ /* CORS note row */ ],        // sibling of the if/else chain
  if (_staleModelNote != null) ...[ /* stale-model note row */ ],
],
```
**New** (`settings_flows.dart`):
```dart
Widget _buildProviderConfigFields(...) {
  if (_isOnDevice) return _buildWebLlmFields(theme);        // line 133 — early return
  if (_isGemma) return _buildGemmaFields(theme);
  if (_isTransformersJs) return _buildTransformersJsFields(theme);
  return _buildStandardFields(theme, selection, corsNote);  // notes only inside here
}
```
`_staleModelNote` is set **exclusively** by the on-device verify paths (`_verifyWebLlmCache`, `_verifyGemmaInstalled`, `_verifyTransformersJsCache` — "cached weights are stale", "N of M installed" warnings) and is reset to null by `_selectProvider`, so it can only be non-null while an on-device provider is selected. By hoisting the notes into `_buildStandardFields` (hosted-only), the extraction made that note unreachable — a real user-facing behavior change in a PR claiming zero behavior change (the note's state setter is now dead UI). The CORS note is structurally dropped the same way but is practically unaffected (`ProviderPreset.cors` returns null for webllm/gemma/transformersJs — verified in `packages/fa_ui/lib/src/providers/provider_preset.dart`). Fix: render `..._buildConfigNotes(theme, corsNote)` after `_buildProviderConfigFields(...)` in `settings.dart` build, as siblings, matching the old tree.

No other issues in the settings split: `_connectHosted` preserves statement order, `mounted` guards, analytics calls, and rememberKey timing; `_applyLastConnection` branch extractions are verbatim; no BuildContext-across-async-gap introduced (all `context.l10n` uses in the extension are pre-await/synchronous); public API (SettingsScreen/AgentSettingsForm/SetupScreen signatures) unchanged; `part 'settings_flows.dart'` registration intact; the `_formSetState` bridge correctly avoids invalid_use_of_protected_member.

# PR #1881 review — UI screens cluster (12 files)

## Findings

### 1. BLOCKING — `flutter_app/lib/ui/screens/settings_flows.dart:133` (+ `settings.dart` build, ~line 873): stale-model note (and structurally the CORS note) no longer rendered for on-device providers

**Old** (`settings.dart` @ 59fb4482ce, `build()`):
```dart
if (!_showProviderListOnly) ...[
  if (_isOnDevice) _buildWebLlmFields(theme)
  else if (_isGemma) _buildGemmaFields(theme)
  else if (_isTransformersJs) _buildTransformersJsFields(theme)

  if (_staleModelNote != null) ...[ /* stale-model note row */ ],
],
```
**New** (`settings_flows.dart`):
```dart

  if (_isOnDevice) return _buildWebLlmFields(theme);        // line 133 — early return
  if (_isGemma) return _buildGemmaFields(theme);
  if (_isTransformersJs) return _buildTransformersJsFields(theme);
```

### 1. BLOCKING — `flutter_app/lib/ui/screens/settings_flows.dart:133` (+ `settings.dart` build, ~line 873): stale-model note (and structurally the CORS note) no longer rendered for on-device providers

**Old** (`settings.dart` @ 59fb4482ce, `build()`):
```dart
if (!_showProviderListOnly) ...[
  if (_isOnDevice) _buildWebLlmFields(theme)
  else if (_isGemma) _buildGemmaFields(theme)
  else if (_isTransformersJs) _buildTransformersJsFields(theme)

],
```
**New** (`settings_flows.dart`):
```dart
Widget _buildProviderConfigFields(...) {
  if (_isOnDevice) return _buildWebLlmFields(theme);        // line 133 — early return
  if (_isGemma) return _buildGemmaFields(theme);
  if (_isTransformersJs) return _buildTransformersJsFields(theme);
  return _buildStandardFields(theme, selection, corsNote);  // notes only inside here
```

# Apps-cluster review — PR #1881 (chore/1848-crap-app-tier4)

Method: per-file patches from the GitHub PR files API (base 59fb4482ce → HEAD dcc6dcff81), cross-checked against full old files (raw.githubusercontent @59fb4482ce) and full new local files. No `part` files involved in this cluster — all extractions are private helpers in the same library, so no part-registration checks apply.

## Findings

### SUGGESTION — dynamic_messages.dart:640 — false doc claim / missed dedup
New code (line ~640):
```dart
/// Cancels the no-UI widgets' timers and drops them (shared by
/// [forgetAll] and [dispose]).
void _cancelNoUiTimers() { ... }
```
But `dispose()` (line ~651) still carries its **own inline copy** of the timer-cancel loop (`for (final timer in _noUiTimers.values) { timer.cancel(); } _noUiTimers.clear();`) and was not touched by the PR (the only hunk is `forgetAll`). The doc comment "shared by [forgetAll] and [dispose]" is factually wrong, and the duplicate loop the extraction should have removed is still there. No behavior change — either fix the doc or make `dispose()` call the helper. (Note: `dispose()` also keeps its deliberately *unawaited* `engine.dispose()` loop, which must NOT be merged into the awaited `_disposeEngines` — only the timer loop is the missed dedup.)

### SUGGESTION — unpacked_load_flow.dart:37-42 — inert reordering of pure constructions
Old: `createFolderPicker()` ran first, and when it returned null the function returned **before** `AppsStore(manager.env)` / `UnpackedWidgetLoader(...)` were constructed. New:
```dart
final store = _unpackedStore(manager, appsStore, loader);
final widgetLoader = _unpackedLoader(manager, store, loader);
await _runUnpackedLoad(...); // createFolderPicker() + null-return inside
```
The fallback `AppsStore(manager.env)` and `UnpackedWidgetLoader(env:, appsStore:)` are now constructed even on the no-op host-can't-pick path. Verified both constructors are pure field initializers (`UnpackedWidgetLoader` ctor: `appsStore = appsStore ?? AppsStore(env)`; `AppsStore` ctor assigns platform/readAsset only), so there is no observable behavior change — but the evaluation order did technically change.

### Observation (not a finding) — unpacked_load_flow.dart
The eager `_unpackedStore` also fixes a latent double-construction asymmetry: old code built `AppsStore(manager.env)` once; new code builds it once and passes it to the loader, identical to old. Injection precedence `loader?.appsStore ?? appsStore ?? AppsStore(...)` is byte-identical to old.

## File-by-file verification (all semantically identical unless noted above)

- **app_preflight_probe_io.dart — CLEAN.** `_probeJsEngineLibrary()` is called inside the same `try` that held the platform branch; `Platform.isMacOS || Platform.isIOS` evaluated once at the same point; the `on ArgumentError` fallback open stays inside the per-call try in `_probeJavaScriptCore` (a throwing fallback still propagates to the outer `on Object` exactly as before — the fallback open lives in the catch clause in both versions); the outer `on Object` catch swallows exactly the same failure set (nothing new escapes, nothing new is swallowed). QuickJS env-var fallback chain unchanged.

### 1. SUGGESTION — `flutter_app/lib/services/relay_agent_service.dart:954` — `mail_routed` now notifies listeners once instead of twice

**Old** (`_onHostEvent` switch, base 59fb4482ce): the `mail_routed` case called `if (!silent) notifyListeners();` inside the case (the "Paint NOW" comment), and then the trailing `if (!silent) notifyListeners();` after the switch fired for ALL event types — so `mail_routed` notified **twice** when live.
**New**: `_onHostMailRoutedEvent` (lines 944–955) contains exactly one `if (!silent) notifyListeners();`, and its caller `_onHostStateEvent` does not notify after the `mail_routed` arm (only the `tool_result`/`status` arm via `_onHostProgressEvent` and the default arm via `_onHostDiagnosticsEvent` notify, once each). All other event types keep the identical single notify; only `mail_routed` changes (2 → 1 `notifyListeners()`). # PR #1881 review — UI screens cluster (12 files)

## Findings

### 1. BLOCKING — `flutter_app/lib/ui/screens/settings_flows.dart:133` (+ `settings.dart` build, ~line 873): stale-model note (and structurally the CORS note) no longer rendered for on-device providers

**Old** (`settings.dart` @ 59fb4482ce, `build()`):
```dart
if (!_showProviderListOnly) ...[
  if (_isOnDevice) _buildWebLlmFields(theme)
  else if (_isGemma) _buildGemmaFields(theme)
  else if (_isTransformersJs) _buildTransformersJsFields(theme)
  else ...[ /* key/model/url fields */ ],
  if (corsNote != null) ...[ /* CORS note row */ ],        // sibling of the if/else chain
  if (_staleModelNote != null) ...[ /* stale-model note row */ ],
],
```
**New** (`settings_flows.dart`):
```dart
Widget _buildProviderConfigFields(...) {
  if (_isOnDevice) return _buildWebLlmFields(theme);        // line 133 — early return
  if (_isGemma) return _buildGemmaFields(theme);
  if (_isTransformersJs) return _buildTransformersJsFields(theme);
  return _buildStandardFields(theme, selection, corsNote);  // notes only inside here
}
```
`_staleModelNote` is set **exclusively** by the on-device verify paths (`_verifyWebLlmCache`, `_verifyGemmaInstalled`, `_verifyTransformersJsCache` — "cached weights are stale", "N of M installed" warnings) and is reset to null by `_selectProvider`, so it can only be non-null while an on-device provider is selected. By hoisting the notes into `_buildStandardFields` (hosted-only), the extraction made that note unreachable — a real user-facing behavior change in a PR claiming zero behavior change (the note's state setter is now dead UI). Fix: render `..._buildConfigNotes(theme, corsNote)` after `_buildProviderConfigFields(...)` in `settings.dart` build, as siblings, matching the old tree.

import 'package:flutter_agent_harness/flutter_agent_harness.dart';

import 'paths.dart';

/// The error/exit pair a utility driver turns into a `_StageResult`.
typedef CommandError = ({String message, int exitCode});

/// The parsed `tar` command line: operation flags, archive, members.
typedef TarInvocation = ({
  bool create,
  bool extract,
  bool compressed,
  String? archiveArg,
  List<String> members,
  String? changeDir,
  CommandError? error,
});

/// Parses the `tar` argument list (pure): old-style `cf` bundling, `-f`,
/// `-C`, and members.
TarInvocation parseTarArgs(List<String> args) {
  if (args.isEmpty) {
    return _tarError('tar: no operation specified\n');
  }
  final (flags, index) = _tarLeadingFlags(args);
  final create = flags.contains('c');
  final extract = flags.contains('x');
  final compressed = flags.contains('z');
  if (create == extract) {
    return _tarError('tar: specify exactly one of -c or -x\n');
  }
  final (archiveArg, next, archiveError) = _tarArchiveArg(args, index, flags);
  if (archiveError != null) return _tarError(archiveError);
  final (changeDir, members) = _tarMembers(args, next);
  if (archiveArg == null) {
    return _tarError('tar: no archive file specified (use -f)\n');
  }
  return (
    create: create,
    extract: extract,
    compressed: compressed,
    archiveArg: archiveArg,
    members: members,
    changeDir: changeDir,
    error: null,
  );
}

/// Extracts the bundled flag cluster from the leading operand (dash form
/// or old-style `cf` letters); returns the flags and whether the leading
/// operand was consumed.
(String, int) _tarLeadingFlags(List<String> args) {
  final first = args.first;
  if (first.startsWith('-')) {
    return (first.substring(1), 1);
  }
  if (RegExp(r'^[a-zA-Z]+$').hasMatch(first) &&
      first.contains(RegExp(r'[ctx]'))) {
    // Old-style `tar cf ...` without a dash.
    return (first, 1);
  }
  return ('', 0);
}

/// The `-f` archive operand, the next scan index, and the usage-error
/// message when the flag's value is missing.
(String?, int, String?) _tarArchiveArg(
  List<String> args,
  int index,
  String flags,
) {
  if (!flags.contains('f')) return (null, index, null);
  if (index >= args.length) {
    return (null, index, 'tar: option requires an argument -- f\n');
  }
  return (args[index], index + 1, null);
}

/// Splits trailing operands into the `-C` change-dir and member paths.
(String?, List<String>) _tarMembers(List<String> args, int index) {
  String? changeDir;
  final members = <String>[];
  for (; index < args.length; index++) {
    final arg = args[index];
    if (arg == '-C' && index + 1 < args.length) {
      changeDir = args[index + 1];
      index++;
    } else {
      members.add(arg);
    }
  }
  return (changeDir, members);
}

TarInvocation _tarError(String message) => (
  create: false,
  extract: false,
  compressed: false,
  archiveArg: null,
  members: const [],
  changeDir: null,
  error: (message: message, exitCode: 2),
);

/// Adds [resolved] (and its children when it is a directory) to [archive],
/// stripping the leading `/` from member names like GNU tar does.
Future<void> addArchiveEntry(
  MemoryFileSystem fs,
  Archive archive,
  String resolved,
  FileInfo info,
) async {
  final name = resolved.startsWith('/') ? resolved.substring(1) : resolved;
  if (info.kind == FileKind.directory) {
    archive.addFile(ArchiveFile('$name/', 0, const <int>[])..isFile = false);
    final entries = await fs.listDir(resolved);
    for (final entry in entries.valueOrNull ?? <FileInfo>[]) {
      await addArchiveEntry(fs, archive, '$resolved/${entry.name}', entry);
    }
    return;
  }
  final data = await fs.readBinaryFile(resolved);
  if (data.isErr) return;
  final bytes = data.valueOrNull!;
  archive.addFile(ArchiveFile(name, bytes.length, bytes));
}

/// Creates the archive at `parsed.archiveArg` from `parsed.members`
/// (`tar c`, optionally gzip-compressed).
Future<CommandError?> createTarArchive(
  MemoryFileSystem fs,
  String cwd,
  TarInvocation parsed,
) async {
  final members = parsed.members;
  if (members.isEmpty) {
    return (
      message: 'tar: Cowardly refusing to create an empty archive\n',
      exitCode: 2,
    );
  }
  final archive = Archive();
  for (final member in members) {
    final resolved = resolveSandboxPath(member, cwd);
    final info = await fs.fileInfo(resolved);
    if (info.isErr) {
      return (
        message: 'tar: $member: Cannot stat: No such file or directory\n',
        exitCode: 1,
      );
    }
    await addArchiveEntry(fs, archive, resolved, info.valueOrNull!);
  }
  var bytes = TarEncoder().encode(archive);
  if (parsed.compressed) bytes = GZipEncoder().encode(bytes);
  await fs.writeBinaryFile(
    resolveSandboxPath(parsed.archiveArg!, cwd),
    Uint8List.fromList(bytes),
  );
  return null;
}

/// Extracts `parsed.archiveArg` into the sandbox (`tar x`, optionally
/// gzip-compressed, honoring `-C`).
Future<CommandError?> extractTarArchive(
  MemoryFileSystem fs,
  String cwd,
  TarInvocation parsed,
) async {
  final archivePath = resolveSandboxPath(parsed.archiveArg!, cwd);
  final read = await fs.readBinaryFile(archivePath);
  if (read.isErr) {
    return (
      message:
          'tar: ${parsed.archiveArg}: Cannot open: No such file or directory\n',
      exitCode: 1,
    );
  }
  var bytes = read.valueOrNull!;
  if (parsed.compressed) {
    try {
      bytes = Uint8List.fromList(GZipDecoder().decodeBytes(bytes));
    } on Object {
      return (
        message: 'tar: ${parsed.archiveArg}: not in gzip format\n',
        exitCode: 1,
      );
    }
  }
  final Archive archive;
  try {
    archive = TarDecoder().decodeBytes(bytes);
  } on Object {
    return (
      message: 'tar: ${parsed.archiveArg}: not in tar format\n',
      exitCode: 1,
    );
  }
  final root = parsed.changeDir != null
      ? resolveSandboxPath(parsed.changeDir!, cwd)
      : resolveSandboxPath('.', cwd);
  for (final file in archive.files) {
    final name = file.name.startsWith('/') ? file.name.substring(1) : file.name;
    if (!file.isFile) {
      await fs.createDir('$root/$name');
      continue;
    }
    await fs.writeBinaryFile('$root/$name', file.content);
  }
  return null;
}

/// The parsed `gzip`/`gunzip` command line.
typedef GzipInvocation = ({
  bool unpack,
  bool keep,
  List<String> files,
  CommandError? error,
});

/// Parses the `gzip`/`gunzip` argument list (pure).
GzipInvocation parseGzipArgs(List<String> args, {required bool decompress}) {
  var unpack = decompress;
  var keep = false;
  final files = <String>[];
  for (final arg in args) {
    if (arg == '-d' || arg == '--decompress' || arg == '--uncompress') {
      unpack = true;
    } else if (arg == '-k' || arg == '--keep') {
      keep = true;
    } else if (RegExp(r'^-[1-9]$').hasMatch(arg)) {
      // Compression level; irrelevant for the in-memory subset.
    } else if (arg.startsWith('-') && arg != '-') {
      return (
        unpack: unpack,
        keep: keep,
        files: files,
        error: (message: 'gzip: unsupported option $arg\n', exitCode: 1),
      );
    } else {
      files.add(arg);
    }
  }
  return (unpack: unpack, keep: keep, files: files, error: null);
}

/// Compresses/decompresses `parsed.files` in place in the sandbox.
Future<CommandError?> runGzip(
  MemoryFileSystem fs,
  String cwd,
  GzipInvocation parsed,
) async {
  final name = parsed.unpack ? 'gunzip' : 'gzip';
  if (parsed.files.isEmpty) {
    return (message: '$name: missing operand\n', exitCode: 1);
  }
  for (final arg in parsed.files) {
    final resolved = resolveSandboxPath(arg, cwd);
    final read = await fs.readBinaryFile(resolved);
    if (read.isErr) {
      return (message: '$name: $arg: No such file or directory\n', exitCode: 1);
    }
    if (!parsed.unpack) {
      final encoded = GZipEncoder().encode(read.valueOrNull!);
      await fs.writeBinaryFile('$resolved.gz', Uint8List.fromList(encoded));
      if (!parsed.keep) await fs.remove(resolved);
      continue;
    }
    if (!resolved.endsWith('.gz')) {
      return (message: 'gzip: $arg: unknown suffix -- ignored\n', exitCode: 1);
    }
    final List<int> decoded;
    try {
      decoded = GZipDecoder().decodeBytes(read.valueOrNull!);
    } on Object {
      return (message: 'gzip: $arg: not in gzip format\n', exitCode: 1);
    }
    final dest = resolved.substring(0, resolved.length - 3);
    await fs.writeBinaryFile(dest, Uint8List.fromList(decoded));
    if (!parsed.keep) await fs.remove(resolved);
  }
  return null;
}

/// The parsed `zip` command line.
typedef ZipInvocation = ({
  bool recursive,
  List<String> positionals,
  CommandError? error,
});

/// Parses the `zip` argument list (pure).
ZipInvocation parseZipArgs(List<String> args) {
  var recursive = false;
  final positionals = <String>[];
  for (final arg in args) {
    if (arg.startsWith('-') && arg != '-') {
      if (arg.contains('r') || arg.contains('R')) recursive = true;
      // Other flags (quiet, compression level, ...) are accepted and
      // ignored by this subset.
    } else {
      positionals.add(arg);
    }
  }
  if (positionals.length < 2) {
    return (
      recursive: recursive,
      positionals: positionals,
      error: (
        message:
            'zip error: Nothing to do! (usage: zip [-r] archive.zip file...)\n',
        exitCode: 1,
      ),
    );
  }
  return (recursive: recursive, positionals: positionals, error: null);
}

/// Zips `positionals[1..]` into the archive `positionals[0]`.
Future<CommandError?> runZip(
  MemoryFileSystem fs,
  String cwd,
  ZipInvocation parsed,
) async {
  final archivePath = resolveSandboxPath(parsed.positionals.first, cwd);
  final archive = Archive();
  for (final member in parsed.positionals.sublist(1)) {
    final resolved = resolveSandboxPath(member, cwd);
    final info = await fs.fileInfo(resolved);
    if (info.isErr) {
      return (
        message:
            'zip error: Nothing to do! ($member: No such file or directory)\n',
        exitCode: 1,
      );
    }
    final fileInfo = info.valueOrNull!;
    if (fileInfo.kind == FileKind.directory && !parsed.recursive) {
      return (
        message: 'zip error: Nothing to do! ($member is a directory; use -r)\n',
        exitCode: 1,
      );
    }
    await addArchiveEntry(fs, archive, resolved, fileInfo);
  }
  final bytes = ZipEncoder().encode(archive);
  await fs.writeBinaryFile(archivePath, Uint8List.fromList(bytes));
  return null;
}

# PR #1881 review — UI screens cluster (12 files)

## Findings

### 1. BLOCKING — `flutter_app/lib/ui/screens/settings_flows.dart:133` (+ `settings.dart` build, ~line 873): stale-model note (and structurally the CORS note) no longer rendered for on-device providers

**Old** (`settings.dart` @ 59fb4482ce, `build()`):
```dart
if (!_showProviderListOnly) ...[
  if (_isOnDevice) _buildWebLlmFields(theme)
  else if (_isGemma) _buildGemmaFields(theme)
  else if (_isTransformersJs) _buildTransformersJsFields(theme)
  else ...[ /* key/model/url fields */ ],
  if (corsNote != null) ...[ /* CORS note row */ ],        // sibling of the if/else chain
  if (_staleModelNote != null) ...[ /* stale-model note row */ ],
],
```
**New** (`settings_flows.dart`):
```dart
Widget _buildProviderConfigFields(...) {
  if (_isOnDevice) return _buildWebLlmFields(theme);        // line 133 — early return
  if (_isGemma) return _buildGemmaFields(theme);
  if (_isTransformersJs) return _buildTransformersJsFields(theme);
  return _buildStandardFields(theme, selection, corsNote);  // notes only inside here
}
```
`_staleModelNote` is set **exclusively** by the on-device verify paths (`_verifyWebLlmCache`, `_verifyGemmaInstalled`, `_verifyTransformersJsCache` — "cached weights are stale", "N of M installed" warnings) and is reset to null by `_selectProvider`, so it can only be non-null while an on-device provider is selected. By hoisting the notes into `_buildStandardFields` (hosted-only), the extraction made that note unreachable — a real user-facing behavior change in a PR claiming zero behavior change (the note's state setter is now dead UI). The CORS note is structurally dropped the same way but is practically unaffected (`ProviderPreset.cors` returns null for webllm/gemma/transformersJs — verified in `packages/fa_ui/lib/src/providers/provider_preset.dart`). Fix: render `..._buildConfigNotes(theme, corsNote)` after `_buildProviderConfigFields(...)` in `settings.dart` build, as siblings, matching the old tree.

No other issues in the settings split: `_connectHosted` preserves statement order, `mounted` guards, analytics calls, and rememberKey timing; `_applyLastConnection` branch extractions are verbatim; no BuildContext-across-async-gap introduced (all `context.l10n` uses in the extension are pre-await/synchronous); public API (SettingsScreen/AgentSettingsForm/SetupScreen signatures) unchanged; `part 'settings_flows.dart'` registration intact; the `_formSetState` bridge correctly avoids invalid_use_of_protected_member.

Method: no shell available, so diffs were reconstructed by reading full NEW files locally and full OLD files fetched from raw.githubusercontent.com at merge-base 59fb4482ce (repo: IstiN/flutter_agent_harness). Verified per file: statement order, loop boundaries, short-circuit/early-return conditions, error paths/strings, closure captures, mutable-state threading, dropped/duplicated statements, defaults, string formatting. No `part`/`part of` splits were introduced in this cluster — all extractions are in-place private helpers, so no registration gaps possible.

## Findings

- **SUGGESTION** — `flutter_app/lib/ui/widgets/apps_panel.dart` ~line 183 (`_calendarReady(calendar)`) and ~line 190 (`_fetchUpcomingEvents(calendar)`): both new helpers declare the `calendar` parameter with no type (implicit `dynamic`). Old code inferred the concrete type from `createCalendarService()` at the use site. Compiles fine (flutter_app's analysis_options is plain `flutter_lints`, no `strict-inference`), but it defeats static checking on `calendar.isAvailable` / `calendar.events(...)` inside the extracted methods and deviates from the file's otherwise fully-typed style. Should be `CalendarApi calendar` (type is imported via `calendar_service.dart`).

## Detail checks the assignment called out

- **span_grid_delegate.dart `_packSpan`** — traced exhaustively, EQUIVALENT. Old inner structure: grow rows (`while (rows.length < cursorRow + h)`) → `fits = cursorCol + w <= crossAxisCount` → `dr`/`dc` scan with `&& fits` short-circuit → mark/add/`cursorCol += w`/break → wrap `if (++cursorCol + w > crossAxisCount) { cursorRow++; cursorCol = 0; }`. New: `_growRows` at the same point in the `while(true)`; `_spanFits` does `if (col + w > crossAxisCount) return false;` (exact negation of the old fits initializer, evaluated before the scan, so the case where `cursorCol` advanced past the row end behaves identically — old loop body ran zero iterations in that case too) then `_rowSegmentOccupied` (same `dc` scan, returns on first occupied, same short-circuit). Row indexing safe: `_growRows` guarantees `rows.length >= cursorRow + h` before `_spanFits` touches `rows[row + dr]`. Wrap condition byte-identical; success path returns `(cursorRow, cursorCol + w)` which the caller destructures — matches old `cursorCol += w; break`. No off-by-one, no infinite-loop change (cursor advancement identical on both paths). `w`/`h` clamping identical.
- **quick_switcher.dart** — contains no fuzzy matching; the recents logic (`_recentNetworkIds`, `i < recents.length && i < 7`, `_digitKeys[i + 3]!`) is untouched. The `_switchTo` change collapses three typed catches into one `on Object` + `_resumeErrorMessage` mapping: StateError→`e.message`, FaNetworkException→`e.message`, else→`'$e'` — same dispatch (the two types are unrelated, so catch order in the old code is preserved by the if-order). `context.mounted` guard moved into `_showResumeError`, checked before every snack, same as old.

Order and all caps/defaults unchanged; image branch correctly converted from early-`return` to if/else (no fall-through added).

# Apps-cluster review — PR #1881 (chore/1848-crap-app-tier4)

Method: per-file patches from the GitHub PR files API (base 59fb4482ce → HEAD dcc6dcff81), cross-checked against full old files (raw.githubusercontent @59fb4482ce) and full new local files. No `part` files involved in this cluster — all extractions are private helpers in the same library, so no part-registration checks apply.

## Findings

### SUGGESTION — dynamic_messages.dart:640 — false doc claim / missed dedup
New code (line ~640):
```dart
/// Cancels the no-UI widgets' timers and drops them (shared by
/// [forgetAll] and [dispose]).
void _cancelNoUiTimers() { ... }
```
But `dispose()` (line ~651) still carries its **own inline copy** of the timer-cancel loop (`for (final timer in _noUiTimers.values) { timer.cancel(); } _noUiTimers.clear();`) and was not touched by the PR (the only hunk is `forgetAll`). The doc comment "shared by [forgetAll] and [dispose]" is factually wrong, and the duplicate loop the extraction should have removed is still there. No behavior change — either fix the doc or make `dispose()` call the helper. (Note: `dispose()` also keeps its deliberately *unawaited* `engine.dispose()` loop, which must NOT be merged into the awaited `_disposeEngines` — only the timer loop is the missed dedup.)

### SUGGESTION — unpacked_load_flow.dart:37-42 — inert reordering of pure constructions
Old: `createFolderPicker()` ran first, and when it returned null the function returned **before** `AppsStore(manager.env)` / `UnpackedWidgetLoader(...)` were constructed. New:
```dart
final store = _unpackedStore(manager, appsStore, loader);
final widgetLoader = _unpackedLoader(manager, store, loader);
await _runUnpackedLoad(...); // createFolderPicker() + null-return inside
```
The fallback `AppsStore(manager.env)` and `UnpackedWidgetLoader(env:, appsStore:)` are now constructed even on the no-op host-can't-pick path. Verified both constructors are pure field initializers (`UnpackedWidgetLoader` ctor: `appsStore = appsStore ?? AppsStore(env)`; `AppsStore` ctor assigns platform/readAsset only), so there is no observable behavior change — but the evaluation order did technically change.

### Observation (not a finding) — unpacked_load_flow.dart
The eager `_unpackedStore` also fixes a latent double-construction asymmetry: old code built `AppsStore(manager.env)` once; new code builds it once and passes it to the loader, identical to old. Injection precedence `loader?.appsStore ?? appsStore ?? AppsStore(...)` is byte-identical to old.

## File-by-file verification (all semantically identical unless noted above)

- **app_preflight_probe_io.dart — CLEAN.** `_probeJsEngineLibrary()` is called inside the same `try` that held the platform branch; `Platform.isMacOS || Platform.isIOS` evaluated once at the same point; the `on ArgumentError` fallback open stays inside the per-call try in `_probeJavaScriptCore` (a throwing fallback still propagates to the outer `on Object` exactly as before — the fallback open lives in the catch clause in both versions); the outer `on Object` catch swallows exactly the same failure set (nothing new escapes, nothing new is swallowed). QuickJS env-var fallback chain unchanged.
- **apps_store.dart — CLEAN.** `_i18nRefsUnchanged` → `_allI18nRefsUnchanged` + `_i18nRefUnchanged`: same `recorded.entries` iteration order, same first-changed short-circuit, same read+digest comparison (`current != null && _digest(current) == entry.value` ≡ `!(current == null || digest != value)`), `recorded == null → true` preserved. Only hunk in the file (+22/−6).
- **catalog_auto_update.dart — CLEAN.** The three passes run in the same order over the same `result.entries`; the shared mutable `updated` list accumulates in identical sequence (pass 1 in-entry order, pass 2 in-entry order, pass 3 skipping `updated.contains(entry.id)` exactly as before); the per-entry try/catch swallow moved into `_reinstallFromCatalog` covers exactly the same statements (download → install → add…

# Review: agent services cluster — PR #1881 (chore/1848-crap-app-tier4)

## Findings

### 1. SUGGESTION — `flutter_app/lib/services/relay_agent_service.dart:954` — `mail_routed` now notifies listeners once instead of twice

**Old** (`_onHostEvent` switch, base 59fb4482ce): the `mail_routed` case called `if (!silent) notifyListeners();` inside the case (the "Paint NOW" comment), and then the trailing `if (!silent) notifyListeners();` after the switch fired for ALL event types — so `mail_routed` notified **twice** when live.
**New**: `_onHostMailRoutedEvent` (lines 944–955) contains exactly one `if (!silent) notifyListeners();`, and its caller `_onHostStateEvent` does not notify after the `mail_routed` arm (only the `tool_result`/`status` arm via `_onHostProgressEvent` and the default arm via `_onHostDiagnosticsEvent` notify, once each). All other event types keep the identical single notify; only `mail_routed` changes (2 → 1 `notifyListeners()`). The double-notify was almost certainly an accident, so the new code is arguably a fix — but it is a literal behavior deviation in a "zero behavior change" PR and should get a one-line callout in the PR description. No rework needed.

## Verified clean (with the specific checks requested)

- **agent_service_events.dart route table** — `_agentEventHandlers` keys are exactly the old switch's 10 cases (AgentStart, TurnStart, MessageUpdate, MessageEnd, ToolExecutionStart, ToolExecutionEnd, ModelRequest, ToolPairingRepair, AgentEnd); unmapped kinds no-op like the old `default: break;`. Field accesses match the old pattern destructuring. Await semantics verified: 8 of 10 handlers are synchronous `void` (signatures checked in the new file), so the `async =>` wrappers complete synchronously; `ModelRequestEvent` and `AgentEndEvent` futures are awaited exactly as the old `await` cases did. No serialization change. `_onToolPairingRepair` early-return guard is the logical inverse of the old `if (nonEmpty && session != null)` — identical.
- **relay_agent_service.dart protocol route table** — covers exactly the 10 mapped old cases; `ToolsPutMsg` and raw hello frames stay no-ops as before. Adapter bodies verbatim (`unawaited(_decideApproval)`, `_sessionsQuery?.complete`, `_error`+notify). Casts are safe (runtimeType-keyed, final-class family); null-safety identical.
- **relay_agent_service.dart `_onHostEvent` split** — outer switch routes exactly `delta/thinking_delta/message_done` to the stream family and everything else to the state family; `error`/`debug`/unknown land in diagnostics (ignore + repaint, matching the old default); no fall-through changes. `_finishAssistant` decomposition preserves the exact branch ladder (error-row early return, tool role, non-assistant roles, empty-assistant placeholder only when no toolCalls, non-empty assistant append+trajectory) and the single final notify.
- **agent_service_sessions.dart** — loadSession's 4-stage split preserves stage order, every `gen != _loadGeneration` checkpoint (as null/false propagation), phase timing computation points, the AppLog summary, and `unawaited(_refreshHistoryAbove())`. The only dropped statement is a duplicate consecutive gen-check with no await between twins — provably a no-op. `_reloadExternalMessages` decomposition preserves reanchor vs append branches, `_growProviderContext` only on plain append, and the torn-read swallow at the same boundary.
- **findReusableSession** — actually lives in `flutter_app/lib/services/flutter_session_manager.dart` (NOT in the assigned agent_service_sessions.dart). Verified there: `newest.createdAt.toLocal()` is preserved (`_isToday(newest.createdAt.toLocal())` with the identical y/m/d vs DateTime.now() comparison); today-check still precedes `_tooLarge` and the message scan; unreadable file still means "do not resume". The claimed toLocal fix is real; no regression.

# PR #1881 review — UI screens cluster (12 files)

## Findings

### 1. BLOCKING — `flutter_app/lib/ui/screens/settings_flows.dart:133` (+ `settings.dart` build, ~line 873): stale-model note (and structurally the CORS note) no longer rendered for on-device providers

**Old** (`settings.dart` @ 59fb4482ce, `build()`):
```dart
if (!_showProviderListOnly) ...[
  if (_isOnDevice) _buildWebLlmFields(theme)
  else if (_isGemma) _buildGemmaFields(theme)
  else if (_isTransformersJs) _buildTransformersJsFields(theme)
  else ...[ /* key/model/url fields */ ],
  if (corsNote != null) ...[ /* CORS note row */ ],        // sibling of the if/else chain
  if (_staleModelNote != null) ...[ /* stale-model note row */ ],
],
```
**New** (`settings_flows.dart`):
```dart
Widget _buildProviderConfigFields(...) {
  if (_isOnDevice) return _buildWebLlmFields(theme);        // line 133 — early return
  if (_isGemma) return _buildGemmaFields(theme);
  if (_isTransformersJs) return _buildTransformersJsFields(theme);
  return _buildStandardFields(theme, selection, corsNote);  // notes only inside here
}
```

```dart
/// Cancels the no-UI widgets' timers and drops them (shared by
/// [forgetAll] and [dispose]).
void _cancelNoUiTimers() { ... }
```
But `dispose()` (line ~651) still carries its **own inline copy** of the timer-cancel loop (`for (final timer in _noUiTimers.values) { timer.cancel(); } _noUiTimers.clear();`) and was not touched by the PR (the only hunk is `forgetAll`). The doc comment "shared by [forgetAll] and [dispose]" is factually wrong, and the duplicate loop the extraction should have removed is still there. No behavior change — either fix the doc or make `dispose()` call the helper. Verified both constructors are pure field initializers (`UnpackedWidgetLoader` ctor: `appsStore = appsStore ?? The eager `_unpackedStore` also fixes a latent double-construction asymmetry: old code built `AppsStore(manager.env)` once; new code builds it once and passes it to the loader, identical to old. Injection precedence `loader?.appsStore ?? appsStore ?? AppsStore(...)` is byte-identical to old.

### 1. SUGGESTION — `flutter_app/lib/services/relay_agent_service.dart:954` — `mail_routed` now notifies listeners once instead of twice

# PR #1881 review — UI screens cluster (12 files)

## Findings

### 1. BLOCKING — `flutter_app/lib/ui/screens/settings_flows.dart:133` (+ `settings.dart` build, ~line 873): stale-model note (and structurally the CORS note) no longer rendered for on-device providers

**Old** (`settings.dart` @ 59fb4482ce, `build()`):
```dart
if (!_showProviderListOnly) ...[
  if (_isOnDevice) _buildWebLlmFields(theme)
  else if (_isGemma) _buildGemmaFields(theme)
  else if (_isTransformersJs) _buildTransformersJsFields(theme)
  else ...[ /* key/model/url fields */ ],
  if (corsNote != null) ...[ /* CORS note row */ ],        // sibling of the if/else chain
  if (_staleModelNote != null) ...[ /* stale-model note row */ ],
],
```
**New** (`settings_flows.dart`):
```dart
Widget _buildProviderConfigFields(...) {
  if (_isOnDevice) return _buildWebLlmFields(theme);        // line 133 — early return
  if (_isGemma) return _buildGemmaFields(theme);
  if (_isTransformersJs) return _buildTransformersJsFields(theme);
  return _buildStandardFields(theme, selection, corsNote);  // notes only inside here
}
```
`_staleModelNote` is set **exclusively** by the on-device verify paths (`_verifyWebLlmCache`, `_verifyGemmaInstalled`, `_verifyTransformersJsCache` — "cached weights are stale", "N of M installed" warnings) and is reset to null by `_selectProvider`, so it can only be non-null while an on-device provider is selected. By hoisting the notes into `_buildStandardFields` (hosted-only), the extraction made that note unreachable — a real user-facing behavior change in a PR claiming zero behavior change (the note's state setter is now dead UI). The CORS note is structurally dropped the same way but is practically unaffected (`ProviderPreset.cors` returns null for webllm/gemma/transformersJs — verified in `packages/fa_ui/lib/src/providers/provider_preset.dart`). Fix: render `..._buildConfigNotes(theme, corsNote)` after `_buildProviderConfigFields(...)` in `settings.dart` build, as siblings, matching the old tree.

No other issues in the settings split: `_connectHosted` preserves statement order, `mounted` guards, analytics calls, and rememberKey timing; `_applyLastConnection` branch extractions are verbatim; no BuildContext-across-async-gap introduced (all `context.l10n` uses in the extension are pre-await/synchronous); public API (SettingsScreen/AgentSettingsForm/SetupScreen signatures) unchanged; `part 'settings_flows.dart'` registration intact; the `_formSetState` bridge correctly avoids invalid_use_of_protected_member.

## Per-file verdicts

| File | Verdict |
|---|---|
| `main.dart` | CLEAN — `MyApp.build` split into `_themeListenable`/`_materialApp`/`_navigatorBuilder`/`_wrapScopes`(+core/model/preview); ListenableBuilder listenable, scope nesting order (FahTheme→packs/sessionKeys/onDevice→media/task→chatText/imagePreviews), and all `BootstrapScreen` args identical. |
| `gemma/gemma_cache_section.dart` | CLEAN — `_scan` split into `_presetRows`/`_presetRow`/`_orphanRows`/`_orphanRow`; row order (presets then orphans), per-row `sizeText` closure capture, and lazy `_storageFrom(dialogContext)` evaluation preserved. |
| `gemma/gemma_stream_function.dart` | CLEAN — switch → `runtimeType` map dispatch is equivalent: `UserMessage`/`ToolResultMessage`/`AssistantMessage` are all `final class` (verified `lib/src/types.dart`, `lib/src/context.dart`), so no subclass can escape the map; truncation logic, ellipsis, and pass-through identical. |
| `transformers_js/transformers_js_stream_function.dart` | CLEAN — engine-unload on error, GPU-crash retry predicate, `startChat` callback wiring, and `throwIfCancelled`/`pushTextEnd`/`pushDone` ordering all preserved verbatim in extracted helpers. |
| `transformers_js/transformers_js_types.dart` | CLEAN — `update()` decomposition keeps the expected-bytes guard, monotonic `_maxFraction`, and the ready/prepare/file status-text mapping identical. |

```dart
/// Cancels the no-UI widgets' timers and drops them (shared by
/// [forgetAll] and [dispose]).
void _cancelNoUiTimers() { ... }
```
But `dispose()` (line ~651) still carries its **own inline copy** of the timer-cancel loop (`for (final timer in _noUiTimers.values) { timer.cancel(); } _noUiTimers.clear();`) and was not touched by the PR (the only hunk is `forgetAll`). final widgetLoader = _unpackedLoader(manager, store, loader);

AppsStore(env)`; `AppsStore` ctor assigns platform/readAsset only), so there is no observable behavior change — but the evaluation order did technically change.

### Observation (not a finding) — unpacked_load_flow.dart
The eager `_unpackedStore` also fixes a latent double-construction asymmetry: old code built `AppsStore(manager.env)` once; new code builds it once and passes it to the loader, identical to old. Injection precedence `loader?.appsStore ?? appsStore ?? AppsStore(...)` is byte-identical to old.

# PR #1881 review — UI screens cluster (12 files)

## Findings

### 1. BLOCKING — `flutter_app/lib/ui/screens/settings_flows.dart:133` (+ `settings.dart` build, ~line 873): stale-model note (and structurally the CORS note) no longer rendered for on-device providers

**Old** (`settings.dart` @ 59fb4482ce, `build()`):
```dart
if (!_showProviderListOnly) ...[
  if (_isOnDevice) _buildWebLlmFields(theme)
  else if (_isGemma) _buildGemmaFields(theme)
  else if (_isTransformersJs) _buildTransformersJsFields(theme)
  else ...[ /* key/model/url fields */ ],
  if (corsNote != null) ...[ /* CORS note row */ ],        // sibling of the if/else chain
  if (_staleModelNote != null) ...[ /* stale-model note row */ ],
],
```
**New** (`settings_flows.dart`):
```dart
Widget _buildProviderConfigFields(...) {
  if (_isOnDevice) return _buildWebLlmFields(theme);        // line 133 — early return
  if (_isGemma) return _buildGemmaFields(theme);
  if (_isTransformersJs) return _buildTransformersJsFields(theme);
  return _buildStandardFields(theme, selection, corsNote);  // notes only inside here
}
```
`_staleModelNote` is set **exclusively** by the on-device verify paths (`_verifyWebLlmCache`, `_verifyGemmaInstalled`, `_verifyTransformersJsCache` — "cached weights are stale", "N of M installed" warnings) and is reset to null by `_selectProvider`, so it can only be non-null while an on-device provider is selected. By hoisting the notes into `_buildStandardFields` (hosted-only), the extraction made that note unreachable — a real user-facing behavior change in a PR claiming zero behavior change (the note's state setter is now dead UI). The CORS note is structurally dropped the same way but is practically unaffected (`ProviderPreset.cors` returns null for webllm/gemma/transformersJs — verified in `packages/fa_ui/lib/src/providers/provider_preset.dart`). Fix: render `..._buildConfigNotes(theme, corsNote)` after `_buildProviderConfigFields(...)` in `settings.dart` build, as siblings, matching the old tree.

No other issues in the settings split: `_connectHosted` preserves statement order, `mounted` guards, analytics calls, and rememberKey timing; `_applyLastConnection` branch extractions are verbatim; no BuildContext-across-async-gap introduced (all `context.l10n` uses in the extension are pre-await/synchronous); public API (SettingsScreen/AgentSettingsForm/SetupScreen signatures) unchanged; `part 'settings_flows.dart'` registration intact; the `_formSetState` bridge correctly avoids invalid_use_of_protected_member.

## Per-file verdicts

| File | Verdict |
|---|---|
| `main.dart` | CLEAN — `MyApp.build` split into `_themeListenable`/`_materialApp`/`_navigatorBuilder`/`_wrapScopes`(+core/model/preview); ListenableBuilder listenable, scope nesting order (FahTheme→packs/sessionKeys/onDevice→media/task→chatText/imagePreviews), and all `BootstrapScreen` args identical. |
| `gemma/gemma_cache_section.dart` | CLEAN — `_scan` split into `_presetRows`/`_presetRow`/`_orphanRows`/`_orphanRow`; row order (presets then orphans), per-row `sizeText` closure capture, and lazy `_storageFrom(dialogContext)` evaluation preserved. |
| `gemma/gemma_stream_function.dart` | CLEAN — switch → `runtimeType` map dispatch is equivalent: `UserMessage`/`ToolResultMessage`/`AssistantMessage` are all `final class` (verified `lib/src/types.dart`, `lib/src/context.dart`), so no subclass can escape the map; truncation logic, ellipsis, and pass-through identical. |
| `transformers_js/transformers_js_stream_function.dart` | CLEAN — engine-unload on error, GPU-crash retry predicate, `startChat` callback wiring, and `throwIfCancelled`/`pushTextEnd`/`pushDone` ordering all preserved verbatim in extracted helpers. |
| `transformers_js/transformers_js_types.dart` | CLEAN — `update()` decomposition keeps the expected-bytes guard, monotonic `_maxFraction`, and the ready/prepare/file status-text mapping identical. |

# PR #1881 review — UI widgets + network cluster (9 files)

Method: no shell available, so diffs were reconstructed by reading full NEW files locally and full OLD files fetched from raw.githubusercontent.com at merge-base 59fb4482ce (repo: IstiN/flutter_agent_harness). Verified per file: statement order, loop boundaries, short-circuit/early-return conditions, error paths/strings, closure captures, mutable-state threading, dropped/duplicated statements, defaults, string formatting. No `part`/`part of` splits were introduced in this cluster — all extractions are in-place private helpers, so no registration gaps possible.

## Findings

- **SUGGESTION** — `flutter_app/lib/ui/widgets/apps_panel.dart` ~line 183 (`_calendarReady(calendar)`) and ~line 190 (`_fetchUpcomingEvents(calendar)`): both new helpers declare the `calendar` parameter with no type (implicit `dynamic`). Old code inferred the concrete type from `createCalendarService()` at the use site. Compiles fine (flutter_app's analysis_options is plain `flutter_lints`, no `strict-inference`), but it defeats static checking on `calendar.isAvailable` / `calendar.events(...)` inside the extracted methods and deviates from the file's otherwise fully-typed style. Should be `CalendarApi calendar` (type is imported via `calendar_service.dart`).

# PR #1881 review — UI screens cluster (12 files)

## Findings

### 1. BLOCKING — `flutter_app/lib/ui/screens/settings_flows.dart:133` (+ `settings.dart` build, ~line 873): stale-model note (and structurally the CORS note) no longer rendered for on-device providers

**Old** (`settings.dart` @ 59fb4482ce, `build()`):
```dart
if (!_showProviderListOnly) ...[
  if (_isOnDevice) _buildWebLlmFields(theme)
  else if (_isGemma) _buildGemmaFields(theme)
  else if (_isTransformersJs) _buildTransformersJsFields(theme)
  else ...[ /* key/model/url fields */ ],
  if (corsNote != null) ...[ /* CORS note row */ ],        // sibling of the if/else chain
  if (_staleModelNote != null) ...[ /* stale-model note row */ ],
],
```
**New** (`settings_flows.dart`):
```dart
Widget _buildProviderConfigFields(...) {
  if (_isOnDevice) return _buildWebLlmFields(theme);        // line 133 — early return
  if (_isGemma) return _buildGemmaFields(theme);
  if (_isTransformersJs) return _buildTransformersJsFields(theme);
  return _buildStandardFields(theme, selection, corsNote);  // notes only inside here
}
```

# PR #1881 review — UI screens cluster (12 files)

## Findings

### 1. BLOCKING — `flutter_app/lib/ui/screens/settings_flows.dart:133` (+ `settings.dart` build, ~line 873): stale-model note (and structurally the CORS note) no longer rendered for on-device providers

**Old** (`settings.dart` @ 59fb4482ce, `build()`):
```dart
if (!_showProviderListOnly) ...[
  if (_isOnDevice) _buildWebLlmFields(theme)
  else if (_isGemma) _buildGemmaFields(theme)
  else if (_isTransformersJs) _buildTransformersJsFields(theme)
  else ...[ /* key/model/url fields */ ],
  if (corsNote != null) ...[ /* CORS note row */ ],        // sibling of the if/else chain
  if (_staleModelNote != null) ...[ /* stale-model note row */ ],
],
```
**New** (`settings_flows.dart`):
```dart
Widget _buildProviderConfigFields(...) {
  if (_isOnDevice) return _buildWebLlmFields(theme);        // line 133 — early return
  if (_isGemma) return _buildGemmaFields(theme);
  if (_isTransformersJs) return _buildTransformersJsFields(theme);
  return _buildStandardFields(theme, selection, corsNote);  // notes only inside here
}
```
`_staleModelNote` is set **exclusively** by the on-device verify paths (`_verifyWebLlmCache`, `_verifyGemmaInstalled`, `_verifyTransformersJsCache` — "cached weights are stale", "N of M installed" warnings) and is reset to null by `_selectProvider`, so it can only be non-null while an on-device provider is selected. By hoisting the notes into `_buildStandardFields` (hosted-only), the extraction made that note unreachable — a real user-facing behavior change in a PR claiming zero behavior change (the note's state setter is now dead UI). The CORS note is structurally dropped the same way but is practically unaffected (`ProviderPreset.cors` returns null for webllm/gemma/transformersJs — verified in `packages/fa_ui/lib/src/providers/provider_preset.dart`). Fix: render `..._buildConfigNotes(theme, corsNote)` after `_buildProviderConfigFields(...)` in `settings.dart` build, as siblings, matching the old tree.

No other issues in the settings split: `_connectHosted` preserves statement order, `mounted` guards, analytics calls, and rememberKey timing; `_applyLastConnection` branch extractions are verbatim; no BuildContext-across-async-gap introduced (all `context.l10n` uses in the extension are pre-await/synchronous); public API (SettingsScreen/AgentSettingsForm/SetupScreen signatures) unchanged; `part 'settings_flows.dart'` registration intact; the `_formSetState` bridge correctly avoids invalid_use_of_protected_member.
